A Christmas special of the BBC comedy-drama Ludwig will see David Mitchell and Anna Maxwell Martin star alongside the likes of Sir David Suchet, Jason Flemyng, Joe Wilkinson and Cathy Tyson.

The show follows Mitchell as John "Ludwig" Taylor, a reclusive puzzle designer who assumes the identity of his missing twin brother, a detective chief inspector.

With the second series of the detective show currently airing and a third series in production, the broadcaster has now confirmed an upcoming seasonal episode.

The festive instalment will see the actor behind one of television’s most famous detectives, Hercule Poirot, having the tables turned, with Sir David taking on the role of a murder suspect.

Other stars who will appear in the special include Utopia actor Alexandra Roach and comedian Kiell Smith-Bynoe.

open image in gallery David Mitchell with Sir David Suchet ( PA )

Set in Yorkshire, the special sees John (Mitchell), Lucy (Maxwell Martin) and her son Henry (Dylan Hughes) arrive at a Christmas-themed hotel for a much-needed escape, until a blackout turns the festivities into a locked-room murder mystery.

Trapped by a blizzard and cut off from the outside world, the guests must spend the night with a killer in their midst.

With John reluctantly pulled into one of his strangest puzzles yet, the race is on for the Taylors to solve the crime before Christmas.

Mitchell said: “I have long been a huge admirer of Sir David Suchet’s work and have watched every episode of Poirot several times, so it was a dream come true for me when he agreed to appear in the Ludwig Christmas special.

“He was an absolute joy to work and spend time with – funny, interesting and generous – and his performance in the programme is wonderful.”

open image in gallery The smash-hit show is created and written by Mark Brotherhood and produced by Big Talk Studios ( BBC/Big Talk )

Sir David added: “It was an absolute pleasure to work alongside David Mitchell and the wonderful ensemble cast.

“It made quite the refreshing change to be playing a suspect rather than the detective, and to sit comfortably in my armchair while David delivered the denouement. I had a thoroughly enjoyable time.”

The first series of Ludwig attracted more than 9.5 million viewers in 28 days and became the BBC’s biggest scripted series since 2024 and the biggest comedy launch episode since at least 2018.

The smash-hit show is created and written by Mark Brotherhood and produced by Big Talk Studios, part of ITV Studios, in association with That Mitchell and Webb Company.

News.title: Burnham risks Truss moment, warn bond traders
News.content:
Andy Burnham risks a Liz Truss-style market meltdown unless he presents a credible plan to pay for his agenda, bond traders have warned.

Investors said the Prime Minister faces further spikes in borrowing costs unless he outlines tax rises or spending cuts to fund his major policies.

UK borrowing costs have surged to multi-decade highs this week amid a global bond market sell-off. However, investors are particularly concerned about Mr Burnham’s fiscal agenda before his first Budget next month.

Al Cattermole, a portfolio manager at Swiss private bank Mirabaud, said investors were “unclear” about the Prime Minister’s plans and how he would pay for them.

He said: “If you have a lack of credibility about your spending plan and how that will be funded, then you would get spikes in yields similar to [what] we saw during the Liz Truss episode.

“That was about unfunded fiscal spending. And if you get that again, then there is concern about that.”

Mr Burnham refused to rule out increasing borrowing during his first Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday despite recent market turmoil.

Jim Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment, said: “Spending cuts are the thing the market wants to hear.

“It would go a long way if this Government were to recognise that it is a challenge that needs addressing – that the path we are on in terms of welfare spending is completely unsustainable.”

He added: “The market knows that, and the market wants to hear that the Government understands that.”

Lord Jim O’Neill said earlier that the Prime Minister must “get real” and cut public spending in order to ease pressure in the bond market.

The cost of long-term government borrowing hit its highest level since 1998 on Wednesday, increasing the strain on the public finances as John Healey, the new Chancellor, prepares for the Budget.

The 10-year gilt yield – a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money – has risen to its highest point since 2007.

News.title: H5N1 hits US mink farms, sparking calls for an urgent cull
News.content:
H5N1 has been detected on a US mink farm for the first time, igniting fears the infected animals could present a human pandemic risk.

The bird flu virus, which has “jumped” from birds to numerous mammal species and infected hundreds of people in recent years, was detected in at least six mink on a farm in Utah in mid-August, according to a notification from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) released over the weekend.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms gives invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate. Mink also have strikingly similar respiratory systems to humans, which greatly increases the human risk.

The animals are farmed for their fur, which is then typically exported to fashion manufacturers in China, Hong Kong, and Russia and used in items like coats and scarves.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 acquires the ability to spread efficiently between people, it could trigger a human pandemic.

“Avian influenza viruses tend to replicate pretty poorly in humans and don’t really have the right sort of properties that allow them to transmit from person to person.

“If H5N1 were to cause a pandemic, it would need to make quite a lot of changes, and there’s a real concern that mink, particularly farmed mink, have a lot of the features that could drive the evolution of H5N1,” Dr Tom Peacock, a virologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

News.title: Collapsing child vaccination in South Africa ‘a public health emergency’
News.content:
Plummeting child immunisation rates are now a public health emergency in South Africa and risk causing outbreaks of preventable but potentially deadly childhood diseases, the government has said.

The proportion of children under one who have received no vaccinations has trebled in the past decade to nearly a third of infants in South Africa.

Mistrust of vaccines and growing ignorance about the benefits of childhood immunisations risk undoing years of progress made by one of the continent’s most effective health systems.

Outbreaks of measles, diphtheria and whooping cough this year have all been linked to poor immunisation rates and are evidence that herd immunity is breaking down, officials warned.

An alert from the department for health said the proportion of unvaccinated infants had hit 36.3 per cent in the first four months of 2026, up from 12.1 per cent in 2017.

The department warned the jump was “effectively tripling the number of completely unvaccinated children and leaving hundreds of thousands of infants at risk of life-threatening illnesses”.

Coverage of the six-in-one hexavalent infant vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, meningitis, and hepatitis B declined from 87 per cent to 60.5 per cent over the same period.

Officials said the shortfall was caused by a lack of people coming forward to bring their children for jabs and was not due to any shortage of vaccines.

Dr Nonhlanhla Ndlovu, deputy director general of South Africa’s health department, told the state broadcaster that parents had a poor understanding of the public health benefits of childhood jabs.

She said: “The second one that comes out is the issue of public trust, in terms of the safety of the vaccines, but also the trust in terms of our systems.”

“Theses vaccines are very safe and we have seen the gains that we have had in our years before and now that is changing.

“The benefit of vaccines far outweigh anything we can talk about in public health. We need them to come back and bring the children for immunisation.”

News.title: Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer
News.content:
It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Julian Alvarez to Barcelona… or Arsenal

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Lamine Camara to Chelsea

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez’s new Man City squad number revealed after £125m Chelsea transfer exit as he’s DENIED old top by ex-Blue
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ’S new squad number at Manchester City has been revealed, but he won’t be wearing a familiar figure.

The Argentine completed a British transfer record transfer worth £125million from Chelsea to City on deadline day.



But Fernandez won’t be seeing his shirt number at Stamford Bridge join him in the move from London to Manchester.

The 25-year-old wore the No8 shirt during his time with the Blues, whom he joined in January 2023 for a then-Premier League record £106m.



However, he has instead taken the No17 shirt with City.

His old No8 shirt is ironically already taken by another former Chelsea star in Mateo Kovacic, who has held the number since 2023/24.



That being said, City’s No17 is nothing to be sneered at.

For over a decade it was worn by another ex-Blues star in Kevin De Bruyne, who between 2015 and 2025 rose to become one of the greatest and most decorated creative midfielders in the history of English football.

The shirt was also worn by the likes of Sun Jihai, Jack Rodwell, Jerome Boateng and Martin Petrov.

Fernandez also stuck the boot into Chelsea by referring to them as his “previous club” – echoing Enzo Maresca‘s refusal to name them – before also saying he had “always dreamed of being at a club as big as City”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “I always dreamed of being at a club as big as City. I’m grateful for the opportunity.

“It’s a very emotional moment for me and my family, to take this step at 25 years old, in a football career that I always dreamed of.

“I can already see just how big the club is. We will enjoy ourselves and win lots of things together.”

The 2022 World Cup winner continued by outlining his targets for the season: “Manchester City have to win every trophy they compete for.



“In every competition we play in, we have to compete and win, because this club’s history demands that.

“To be honest, from the first day they believed in me and called me to say they wanted me to join the club, I didn’t hesitate for a second.

“It’s a club that has won a lot in recent years. It’s a club that is making history in football and, for me, it’s a huge challenge.

“To be able to come here, help the club and keep winning things together, that has been my goal since they called me: to come to this club knowing we are going to win many trophies together.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fernandez could make his Man City debut this weekend in front of his new home crowd when they host Frank Lampard‘s newly-promoted Coventry.

City are top of the league after beating Bournemouth and Crystal Palace, while Coventry sit in 17th after losing to Arsenal and Hull.

Sports.title: Mbappe at centre of kidnap plot after gangster, 18, ‘masterminded attacks on 26 footballers, rappers & business moguls’
Sports.content:
TWISTED PLOT Mbappe at centre of kidnap plot after gangster, 18, ‘masterminded attacks on 26 footballers, rappers & business moguls’

A TEENAGER has been arrested for plotting the abduction of Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé and other wealthy individuals in France, it has been reported.

Clément L, 18, has been labelled as the mastermind of a gang he allegedly operated through Snapchat, under the alias “Lester Z”, while in prison for pimping and armed robbery.



Trawling through his two mobile phones, authorities found addresses and information linked to 26 targets.

Mbappé. who boasts an estimated net worth of around £200million, is the most prominent of them.



Rappers and businessmen, including a Turkish meat trader and a jeweller, all with enormous fortunes were also marked by the gang.

The plot began to unravel when two alleged gang members armed with handguns robbed a watchmaker’s shop in Paris in May, according to Le Parisien.

The pair made off with 11 luxury watches worth £128,000 before fleeing the scene on a scooter.

One suspect was arrested half an hour later after crashing his two-wheeler into a truck, and a second was arrested shortly after.

The investigation eventually led police to Clément and an accomplice.

“This young man was already in prison for serious offenses, and now he is turning up in a new case involving a rapper and a renowned footballer,” the Advocate General told the court this morning.



“Only solitary confinement in prison can make him understand the reality of the situation, given the chaotic, criminal life he leads.”

Clément’s criminal record includes two convictions for drug-related offences and one for violent robbery.

He dropped out of school while studying for a vocational qualification in cooking, it was reported.



“I know the offences are serious,” the young man told the court.

During questioning, he attempted to downplay his level of involvement in the gang.

So far, Clément maintains that he was not the mastermind – but merely an intermediary between a mysterious boss and the foot soldiers who carried out the act.

In his defence, he said: “I’m being held in solitary confinement, surrounded by madmen and terrorists, and I don’t think that’s going to improve.

“I really want to become a chef; it’s been a dream of mine since I was very young.”

Sports.title: New £4million football stadium is coming to UK seaside town – as club to return home for first time in 40 years
Sports.content:
PLANS for a brand new £4million football stadium in a UK seaside town are set to be approved.

The project would see the ground, which was once home to a football club, host the team for the first time in 40 years.



The proposals, which look set to be given the green light by Great Yarmouth Council, outline plans for a new Gorleston FC stadium.

The Norfolk-based Isthmian League team currently play at Wellesley Road Stadium but their original home ground was at Gorleston Recreation Ground.



The football club plan to use the site for a £4million regeneration project that will see full-sized 3G pitch, stands, floodlights and a clubhouse built.

The ground would also feature changing rooms as well as a bar and cafe onsite.

Plans for the stadium at the Recreation Ground, where Gorleston FC last played in 1982, would allow for a maximum capacity of 1,300 spectators.

Although councillors are expected to back the proposals at next week’s meeting, some locals have objected to the development.

Residents have raised concerns over noise levels and the loss of outdoor space for the community, as well as parking issues.

However, the majority of locals are in favour of the plan, with over 400 showing support for the scheme.



It is hoped that the new stadium will boost the area’s economy, provide new jobs and encourage community and youth football.

It’s thought that the risk of noise complaints will be mitigated by limiting use of the pitch to certain times of day, with no play between 10:15pm and 8am.

Sports.title: Argentina villain Leandro Paredes hints at international retirement after 10-game ban
Sports.content:
Argentina villain Leandro Paredes hints at international retirement after 10-game ban

Leandro Paredes was hit with a 10-game ban following his vile behaviour after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain and he has suggested that he may never represent his country again

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has hinted he could retire from international duty (Image: Getty Images)

Argentina’s Leandro Paredes has hinted that he could retire from international duty after being slapped with a 10-match ban. The Boca Juniors midfielder sparked an ugly brawl after the South American nation’s World Cup final defeat by Spain.

‌



He shoved Spain star Gavi to the floor and faced three FIFA assault charges. After an investigation, FIFA handed him a 10-match ban and Paredes has now suggested that he might have made his last appearance for his country due that suspension, as well as Lionel Messi’s decision to hang up his boots for Argentina.

‌



“It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,” Paredes said. “Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision... It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

‌



“I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Paredes, 32, has made 84 appearances in all for Argentina during his career, having made his debut back in 2017. He has also represented Roma, Zenit, PSG, Juventus and Roma.

‌



His comments come after he took aim at FIFA for their ban. He said: "That seems excessive to me. It is also strange that Gavi only received a suspension, even though he struck me in the chest. But well, that's how it is now. We now have to appeal against the sanction.

"The people who know about these things will see whether they can overturn it. For me, it is excessive and I think it can be reduced."

View 2 Images Paredes was involved in an angry brawl after the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, he has also commented on Messi’s decision to retire from international duty following the World Cup defeat. He said: “Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled.

“We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.”

Messi retires having made 207 appearances for Argentina in over 20 years and in that time, he has netted 125 goals. He helped the South American side to the World Cup in Qatar four years ago and has also won the Copa America twice. Messi has also claimed the Ballon d’Or on eight occasions during his lengthy career.

Premier League spending has become a laughing stock - implosion will surely follow

Three Prime Ministers have come and gone since Manchester City were charged with breaking spending rules - and their spending this summer underlines the problem

View 3 Images Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak continues to spend, spend, spend (Image: Getty Images)

Richard Masters has had better weeks. Because he’s just been forced to sit and watch a product he runs eat itself from the inside out.

‌



A product which has spent millions on legal fees attempting to hold Manchester City to account. A club accused of breaking Premier League spending rules.

‌



So concerned with being found guilty, however, that it decided to spend the thick end of another £200million on new signings in the final hours of the summer transfer window.

‌



The world of football is still waiting to discover the outcome of the investigation into City’s alleged wrongdoings. So long, in fact, that in the time it has taken the relevant authorities to charge them with an offence and fail to reach a verdict, the UK has had three different Prime Ministers.

And none of them have had the wit to intervene in solving one of the most farcical events a game which England invented has ever been put through.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



In the meantime, City have taken the liberty of breaking their own spending record on a player not once, but twice, in the same summer.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez joined Manchester City for £125m on deadline day (Image: Manchester City FC)

It’s safe to assume the likes of Enzo Fernandez wouldn’t be joining City if they stood a serious chance of being punished with relegation to the lower leagues. It’s safe to assume Elliot Anderson wouldn’t be joining City if they stood a chance of being punished with relegation to the lower leagues.

‌



Get my drift? The integrity of the Premier League is becoming shambolic. It has become a laughing stock.

Liverpool broke their own transfer record twice last summer. Tottenham have spent more than £300m this summer and are still yet to win a league game.

View 3 Images Premier League CEO Richard Masters must know the integrity of his competition is being seriously questioned (Image: PA)

‌



Everton were willing to spend £10m on a loan fee for Joshua Zirkzee, who has been about as threatening at Manchester United as a wet sponge. Aston Villa won the Europa League, got into the Champions League, then decided to flog all their best players.

But signed someone in Alejandro Garnacho who stunk out United and then Chelsea. Go figure? The panic clubs show, which are run by executives being paid huge salaries in return for their so-called expertise, is frightening.

Who in their right mind thinks Fernandez is worth £125m? No-one, apart from those who treat hard cash like it's come from a Monopoly box. The same people who thought Anderson was worth £116m plus extras.

Article continues below

The footballing world has gone mad. City are not the only ones to blame. Top flight clubs have smashed their summer transfer record with over £3.3bn spent. More than half of them broke their transfer records in a window featuring four of the top flight's five most expensive ever deals.

Perpetuating a market which now sees clubs indulge in the kind of financial spending, which leaves those living in the real world wondering when it will all implode on itself.

Sports.title: Premier League transfers rated and slated after record-breaking summer of spending
Sports.content:
The summer transfer window is over and a record £3.49billion was spent across the Premier League, with over £500m of that coming just on deadline day itself.

Transfer fees of over £100m have become commonplace in the Premier League, with Enzo Fernandez (£125m from Chelsea to Manchester City), Bradley Barcola (£123m from Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (£117m from Aston Villa to Chelsea), Elliot Anderson (£116 from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) and Sandro Tonali (£100m from Newcastle to Tottenham) all reaching that mark.

Eleven of the 20 clubs in the Premier League broke their transfer record this summer, with City the biggest spenders, splashing out £458m on new players - another record for a single window. Chelsea (£349m) and Tottenham (£302m) went big this summer, while newly-promoted Ipswich spent a staggering £171m.

All this spending doesn't guarantee success. There are bound to be some high-profile flops this season, while some clubs managed to miss out on their targets altogether. Here Mirror Football's reporters give their takes on the busiest summer of spending ever.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

John Cross

Which team had the best window?

Manchester City. Enzo Maresca is trying to take over from Pep Guardiola, the best manager in Premier League history. He has to put his stamp on this team. They let legends go but have now brought in top, top quality. Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Iliman Ndiaye and the rest. They also got good prices on their sales. They must be laughing all the way to the bank with Savio. City now look like a team equipped to challenge for the title again.

Which team had the worst window?

Everton. No wonder the fans are up in uproar. I was looking at Crystal Palace and Fulham … but the way it ended for Everton leaves us in no doubt. They lost their talisman in Iliman Ndiaye. They could not get Folarin Balogun over the line. They look short of numbers, they look worse off and it’s going to be hard for David Moyes to progress this season.

Best signing?

Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal took Newcastle’s club captain, their best player and a ready made Premier League midfield superstar and got him for £75m. The best midfield just got better. It’s great value and also you are adding quality in a crazy market. If only Arsenal had got a left winger, too…

‌



View 8 Images Bruno Guimaraes was Arsenal's most expensive signing this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

Most over-rated signing?

Savio. Tottenham paid how much?! They overpaid on a raft of deals but this one stuck out by a mile. Sandro Tonali for £100m was huge. Mateus Fernandes at £85m? Are you sure? Well, Savio who rarely did anything but flatter to deceive is the biggest price of all. Yes, they had to pay big to get good players after two successive 17th place finishes. But wow.

Best value for money signing?

Emiliano Martinez. He is fantastic business at £7.5m. A World Cup winner, a top class keeper at great value who is a game-changer for Chelsea. Robert Sanchez was not good enough and needed replacing. But they also have Mike Penders coming through. They can’t block his progress. This is just perfect and makes Chelsea potential title winners.

Which player are you most excited to see?

Bradley Barcola. The Frenchman has great stats for goals, assists and goal involvements generally. But if you actually watch him - remember watching games?! - then you will know that he can be frustrating and waste openings and chances. This is his big stage to deliver and I feel Liverpool are buying potential but also a player with a big to prove. And that’s good news. The other one is Mykhailo Mudryk. It’s a fascinating story.

‌



View 8 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's big-money signing this summer (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Andy Dunn

Which team had the best window?

If there is an Agents XI out there, they stormed this category. The Premier League’s Deadline Day is their Christmas Day - and then some.

‌



It is tempting to see Manchester City as the big winners but any club that loses Rodri in a window cannot go lighting up the cigars. They might have got thumped at Old Trafford last weekend but I like the look of Ipswich Town’s business. Before their summer trading, they would have been seen as certainties for a relegation fight but the late capture of Zian Flemming completed a successful window.

Which team that had the worst window?

It was Everton, obviously. After all, the worst-window competition is the only thing they have won in the past three decades. And they have won it regularly. Even so, to leave the manager with only one striker - and that striker being Thierno Barry - was spectacularly inept.

But a special mention should go to their neighbours. It is hard to say a window has been bad for a team that signed a £123m player from Paris Saint-Germain but Bradley Barcola is not what Liverpool needed. A central midfielder and a right-back were needed and did not arrive.

View 8 Images Everton are very short after a miserable window (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Best signing?

Considering the amount of money that is circulated, it is easy to be cynical about the transfer window, but there are some high-quality players moving for new challenges. Forget the price tag, Morgan Rogers is a brilliant acquisition for Chelsea and will ensure the anticipated title challenge materialises. James Trafford represents a game-changing piece of business for Leeds United but the signing that could well prove to be stellar is Ayyoub Bouaddi. It cost them enough money but Manchester City have a superstar on their hands.

Most overrated signing?

This is a fiercely-contested category with plenty of candidates - and that is before we look beyond Tottenham Hotspur. Enzo Fernandez has become the first player to be transferred twice for fees of over £100m, which considering the baggage he brings and his limitations, is staggering. Liverpool have paid plenty for Bradley Barcola and Nottingham Forest ’s £50m for Liam Delap was distinctly excessive. But the most overrated and over-priced has to be Sandro Tonali. At £100m, it is hard to know what Spurs were thinking.

View 8 Images Sandro Tonali is the most expensive of Tottenham's summer signings (Image: Getty Images)

Best value-for-money signing?

It is tempting to hail Emi Martinez - at £7.5m - as the bargain of the window but that might make the new Chelsea keeper even more unbearable, so we’ll park that. His fellow keeper, James Trafford, was an absolute snip at £40million for Leeds United and the same can be said for Hull City ’s £20m recruit in the same position, Konstantinos Tzolakis. But on the limited evidence of the season so far, Mamadou Sangare - who cost Brentford less than £40million - looks like the best pound-for-pound signing of the window.

‌



Player you're most excited to see at new club?

Manchester City fans will love Ayyoub Bouaddi’s style and although Evertonians will not be too buoyant right now, Hayden Hackney’s progress should give them some positivity over the coming months.

Abdul Fatawu has already proven to be good to watch with Ipswich and despite reservations about the size of his transfer fee, Bradley Barcola’s progress will be intriguing. But simply because we don’t know what to expect, it will be fascinating to see what Matias Fernandez-Pardo can do at Newcastle United.

Jeremy Cross

Which team had the best window?

Chelsea bucked their status quo of recent times and actually did some of the best business.

The signing of Morgan Rogers is one to excite the fans, as is landing Emi Martinez, while Chelsea also managed to off-load Mykhailo Mudryk on loan and recoup a whopping £125m for troublemaker Enzo Fernandez. The comings and goings have been astonishing, even by Chelsea's standards, but the net result is a stronger and more balanced squad, on the back of still making a profit.

‌



View 8 Images Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea from Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Which team had the worst window?

Aston Villa have had a summer to forget, which is baffling considering they won the Europa League to reach the Champions League. Heroes have vanished in the shape of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Martinez and Ollie Watkins. Villa have made some signings, but it's hard to see any of them replacing the quality which has gone. The strategy has been too drastic to allow Unai Emery to compete for a trophy and retain a place in the top four this season. Shambolic.

Best signing?

Emi Martinez has cost Chelsea just £7.5m, which in today's market, is peanuts. In return, Chelsea have got themselves one of the best goalkeepers in the business.

When it comes to signing keepers, Chelsea's recent record has been embarrassing. But they've struck gold this time. Martinez has all the experience in the world, having played in two World Cup finals and won one of them. He will make Chelsea much harder to beat.

‌



View 8 Images Emi Martinez has become the latest star to move from Aston Villa to Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Most over-rated signing?

The answer to this is simple. Savio runs him close, but Enzo Fernandez cost Manchester City a club-record £125m, which is mind boggling considering he's never challenged for a league title at Chelsea.

Fernandez is a decent footballer, but he's no Roy Keane or Patrick Vieira. What he actually is, is overpriced and overhyped. The fact he's now cost two English clubs more than £100m speaks volumes for how the game has lost its marbles, when it comes to the transfer market.

Best value for money signing?

Mamadou Sangare is starting to resemble the most underrated signing of the summer. The midfielder, 24, has joined Brentford from Lens in a club record £39m deal. But in years to come the fee might feel like some of the best money ever spent by a Premier League club. The Mali international is already making an impact in the Premier League and is guaranteed to prove a heck of a bargain.

‌



View 8 Images Mamadou Sangare has made a bright start at Brentford (Image: Getty Images)

Which player are you most excited to see?

Carlos Baleba hasn't come cheap, having joined Manchester United from Brighton in a £70m deal. But during his time on the south coast, Baleba showed signs he could go on to become a truly world-class midfielder. He appears to be the box-to-box star United have been missing in recent times. Could he become the next Roy Keane? United is a demanding environment, but it will be fun seeing how he adapts to his new surroundings at a club where times are never dull.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso and Lamine Camara phone call as Monaco chief risks Chelsea wrath with statement
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso and Lamine Camara phone call as Monaco chief risks Chelsea wrath with statement

Chelsea missed out on AS Monaco's Lamine Camara late on deadline day and now face fierce competition for his signature next year.

View Image Lamine Camara saw a move to Chelsea collapse

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso spoke directly to Lamine Camara after the transfer collapsed on deadline day, while Monaco's sporting director has since told the midfielder he will have 'even better options soon.' The Blues found themselves seeking for a new midfielder once it became clear that Enzo Fernandez was heading to Manchester City.

‌



After seeing two bids rejected by Monaco, Chelsea finally made a breakthrough and were closing in on a £47.1million deal for Camara - before the plug was pulled at the eleventh hour. Camara was in the middle of his medical at a private clinic when he was abruptly told the move had been scrapped, after Folarin Balogun's transfer to Everton collapsed for a second time.

‌



Problems were first raised during the striker's medical, prompting talks to be paused before later being revived. But in the end, Balogun decided against joining Everton, leaving Monaco's plans in tatters.

‌



Chelsea were left furious by the collapse, with Alonso now short in midfield, even if Fernandez had been sidelined for much of the early season amid uncertainty over his future.

Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro admitted Camara had asked to leave, but said he has since spoken to the midfielder and reassured him that a major move will come 'very soon' - adding that he could have 'even better options than he did yesterday,' a pointed remark towards Chelsea.

"Our priority was to keep Lamine in the club, it's going to be his third season, normally the cycle we do we try to protect our solid performers because the performances are strongly connected to the financial situation of the club," Scuro admitted. "Clearly, we were open to discussing a transfer for Balogun, he finished his third season, we were already working to replace him, we were fully ready to do this.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

"To talk about Lamine, we have been approached by several clubs during the summer, the message has always been the same that our priority is that he stays, even yesterday morning after the training session, we had a conversation with Lamine directly which was very okay and friendly, where he also showed the desire to stay, that he was happy at the club, adapted to this."

Liverpool also made contact with the Ligue 1 side and may be tempted to sign him in the future, potentially next summer.

‌



Camara has now rejoined Monaco training and is back working alongside his team‑mates. Reports in France say he looked fully focused in training and even received a 'warm embrace' from his team‑mates during the warm‑up, as Monaco stepped up preparations for their clash with Paris Saint‑Germain.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Monaco chief also outlined how both deals collapsed, setting out the extraordinary chain of events in detail.

‌



"At this moment at 4pm, Balo was in Liverpool making his medicals. Everything was going pretty well," Scuro added. "At around 7pm we were contacted by Everton raising questions on the medicals of Balo, which for our medical staff, which for the personal medical staff of the player, there was totally no sense.

"The explanations were not enough to justify or to bring concerns of the future of the player. This discussion started between medical departments from here and there. It took forever, about two to three hours, to go deep on the assessment check with other doctors. This is a normal situation when the doctor of the club raises concerns. It's quite normal that clubs will look for other specialists sharing the images and discuss the case.

"Meanwhile, as everything on the last day, this was in the press quite quickly. I would say around half an hour after we were contacted, it was already in the media that Balo is failing on the medical. Then Chelsea saw the opportunity. Okay, Monaco needs money. Balo is struggling there. Let's go. Let's try. And this is the game. It's fair to play this game. There is no problem. Chelsea came and said 'here, I can be here for the solution'. And on this moment, we had to open the door for the discussion.

‌



"We started to open negotiations with Chelsea for Lamine. I informed the player directly myself. I called him. I informed his agent as we always do. Very open. We had discussions between the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea. At the same time, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balo. And what happened was that around 10pm in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that okay, there's no problem. We are ready to do let's sign the contract.

Scuro continued: "Chelsea was always testing and trying. 'What about Lamine? What about Lamine?' I've been talking to them from the last 10 days. As soon as we got the information, yes, we did came back to Chelsea and told 'okay, we have our deal there'. There is no deal on Lamine because it's also fair to do this. It's also part of the game.

‌



"There's no reason that this kind of discussions or dynamic on the last day of the transfer window which all of us decided to be on the last day trying to find solutions with the clock ticking in our neck that now this kind of interaction becomes the bad guys in the room that Monaco is not fair, Monaco is not right. Everybody is very fair and nice in football industry just Monaco is not too much. So this is the storytelling."

Roma midfielder Manu Kone was another target high on Chelsea's wishlist, but the Blues failed to land the Frenchman, who impressed at the World Cup. Chelsea were close to an agreement for Kone, yet Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini was determined to keep hold of him, according to Sky in Italy.

Sports.title: Every Premier League club's transfer window graded as Man Utd, Liverpool and Arsenal shown up
Sports.content:
The biggest summer transfer window in Premier League history has reached its conclusion. A rollercoaster window packed with long transfer sagas, sudden departures and shock U-turns saw top-flight clubs smash the transfer spending record for a single window.

The combined £3.48billion expenditure surpassed the previous £3.14bn record set last year. Clubs also recouped £2.17bn from player sales, contributing to a combined net spend of £1.3bn. Playing a key part in that were big spenders Manchester City (£440.3m), Chelsea (£342.4m) and Tottenham (£334m), and it is no surprise that they enjoyed the best windows across the big clubs.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United signed some crucial players for large sums too, but ultimately ended the window somewhat disappointed for various reasons. The other clubs have been busy too, meaning we can expect an even more competitive league season, with the battle for Europe to be tighter than ever.

Here, Mirror Football examines the transfer business conducted by every Premier League club this summer and grades them based on whether they have addressed key areas and ultimately improved.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Enzo Fernandez completes record Man City transfer continuing Premier League trend READ MORE :

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Arsenal: B-

The champions added considerable depth this summer which has undoubtedly strengthened Mikel Arteta’s squad. Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes add another layer of elite quality and flexibility to the Gunners’ defence and midfield, respectively, while Illan Meslier is a respectable back-up option to David Raya. Christos Tzolis gives Arteta another option out wide, bringing Arsenal’s total spending to around £200m, including the permanent signing of Piero Hincapie which was agreed last year.

But there is understandably concern that Arsenal failed to address their biggest need - elevating their attack by signing a world-class forward - having ultimately fallen short in their pursuits of Morgan Rogers, Kenan Yildiz, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. With fine margins often deciding the title, failing to secure a top hitman could prove critical.

‌



Sporting director Andrea Berta was successful in moving on Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Fabio Vieira, Christian Norgaard, Reiss Nelson and Ethan Nwaneri, but there are question marks over how Arsenal could lose so many forwards and only bring in Tzolis.

View 13 Images Bruno Guimaraes was Arsenal's most expensive signing this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

Aston Villa: B

Villa have undergone quite the rebuild, with Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Ibrahim Mbaye and Joao Gomes among a very expensive group of arrivals, while Leon Goretzka on a free could prove particularly shrewd. Plenty more quality has been added too with the likes of Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho, giving Unai Emery options across the pitch.

But there is little escaping the fact that such an overhaul was triggered by a mass exodus of players joining bigger clubs - Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Emi Martinez all joined traditional ‘big six’ teams, while Ollie Watkins left for Saudi Arabia. It will take a monumental task for Emery to integrate all of his new players and still challenge in the Premier League and the Champions League this season. The biggest credit to Villa is that, while they had little control over key players wanting to leave, they at least seem to have done a stellar job in replacing them.

‌



Bournemouth: B

Defender Antonio Silva is the standout addition and could prove excellent value if he develops as hoped under Marco Rose, while Alvaro Rodriguez and Juanlu Sanchez add further upside and Michele Di Gregorio strengthens the goalkeeping options. Just as importantly, the Cherries resisted interest in Alex Scott and Eli Junior Kroupi and have not ripped apart a side now facing the additional demands of European football.

Marcos Senesi leaving for Tottenham was a clear blow, while Luis Sinisterra, Enes Unal and Hamed Traore have also moved on. It was by no means a remarkable window for Bournemouth and injuries may leave the squad a little light across four competitions, but key pieces were largely protected and the recruitment again looks coherent.

View 13 Images (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Brentford: A

Mamadou Sangare and El Hadji Malick Diouf are exactly the sort of ambitious yet shrewd signings Brentford have built their model around, even at relatively substantial fees, while Jaidon Anthony and Jannik Schuster strengthen the depth. Callum Wilson is also a low-risk free transfer who offers an experienced option in attack.

‌



Ethan Pinnock, Frank Onyeka and Jordan Henderson would have been tough to lose but none of the departures are the sort of damaging ‘stripping of the squad’ Brentford have experienced in previous summers. They have retained their most important assets while strengthening several areas, making this one of the most complete individual windows in the Premier League.

View 13 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Brighton: B+

Brighton very rarely disappoint when it comes to finding creative options in the transfer window and they didn’t disappoint this summer either. Luka Vuskovic is an eye-catching £50m addition and the Seagulls have also added Pascal Struijk, Chema Andres, Jaouen Hadjam and Costinha to their ranks. There are enough first-team-ready additions among the usual assortment of young prospects to suggest there was clear succession planning behind their business.

They certainly needed it, because Carlos Baleba and Jan Paul van Hecke were two huge departures and Danny Welbeck’s move to Chelsea removes another experienced and influential figure. Brighton have once again managed to generate big money while backing themselves to replace their best players before their value peaks. However, losing that much established quality prevents them from receiving a higher grade.

‌



Chelsea: A-

View 13 Images Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea from Aston Villa earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Morgan Rogers was one of the outstanding players in the Premier League last season and gives Chelsea another elite attacking option, while Maxence Lacroix addresses the defence and Emiliano Martinez finally offers capable hands in goal. Those deals alone dramatically improve the spine of Xabi Alonso’s team. Meanwhile, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha and Valentin Barco continue the club’s investment in younger talent, with Welbeck and Henderson adding some much-needed experience in the dressing room.

Chelsea’s ability to extract enormous fees was just as impressive, with Enzo Fernandez sold to Manchester City for £125m and significant money being raised through Nicolas Jackson, Marc Cucurella, Liam Delap, Andrey Santos, Trevoh Chalobah and Tyrique George’s exits. The Blues continue to pursue a bizarre model that constantly has a high player turnover. Though, financially at least, it seems to work. Missing out on a final midfield target takes some shine off their window but it was not for want of trying, having agreed a deadline day transfer for Lamine Camara only for Monaco to pull out of the deal. Alonso will hope his current midfielders can stay injury free until January.

Coventry City: C-

You have to spend to have a fighting chance of staying in the top flight and Coventry can’t be accused of not doing that, breaking their transfer record more than once. But while the likes of Sunderland have seen it pay off, it feels like Coventry are still significantly lacking.

‌



There’s no room for sentiment at the top table - would other clubs in the survival scrap have signed Carl Rushworth and Gus Hamer? No. Frank Lampard would be within his rights to feel like Doug King could’ve backed him more and he’ll have to work his magic to have a glimmer of hope to not be playing Championship football again next season.

Crystal Palace: D

Palace struggled to juggle their domestic and European commitments last season. They’re now playing in the Europa League rather than the Conference League with a worse squad, and the players they didn’t sell still want out anyway.

Their incomings are a worrying read. Ben Chilwell and Takehiro Tomiyasu both joined on a free, which feels very 2023. Anan Khalaili has big shoes to fill after Daniel Munoz departed, and Quinten Timber and Zavier Gozo are the only other signings with a fee.

And that’s before you get to perhaps the worst swap deal in the history of swap deals, Dwight McNeil for Brennan Johnson. Steve Parish was lucky to have Oliver Glasner - he'd better hope Pierre Sage is as good at pulling off minor miracles.

‌



View 13 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Everton: D

Jack Grealish returning for another loan spell is the obvious headline and Tyrique George, Hayden Hackney and Merlin Rohl are useful long-term additions, with Christian Norgaard bringing experience in midfield and Brennan Johnson another attacking option. In isolation there is plenty to like about several of those deals, with the squad looking far healthier before the final hours of deadline day.

But selling Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City for £65m and allowing Beto to leave would only have made sense if Everton had completed the striker signing they were after. However, the failed move for Folarin Balogun was borderline farcical, with the American pulling the plug on the deal. Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam and Nathan Patterson also left, leaving Everton short of numbers and, most damagingly, short of a recognised striker after weakening the attack at the last possible moment.

View 13 Images Iliman Ndiaye's move to Man City is a huge blow for Everton (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

‌



Fulham: D-

It’s always a red flag when a club’s recruitment strategy is 95% signing players from the manager’s former club(s). See Exhibit A: Erik ten Hag at Manchester United. As if the inexperience of Alvaro Arbeloa wasn’t a concern enough, making his side the Cottagers Castilla really does set the alarm bells ringing.

Arbeloa signed three youngsters from Real Madrid in Gonzalo Garcia, Cesar Palacios and Manuel Angel. Signing from Real Madrid usually get fans excited. Those names do not.

About 40% of Fulham's Premier League goals were scored by Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez last season but they both departed. There’s going to have to be some serious stepping up and contributions from across the pitch.

Hull City: B+

It’s never easy being the play-off promoted team and already being a couple of weeks behind in terms of preparing for the step up. Football’s played on grass, yes, but Hull were also massive overperformers when looking at the data last season. And then they had financial regulation fears to contend with after winning at Wembley.

‌



With all that factored in, the Tigers have done pretty well this summer. They’ve leaned into the quantity over quality approach, Nottingham Forest-esque.

The signing of Christos Mouzakitis, dubbed 'the next Luka Modric' and attracting attention from Europe's top teams, is particularly eye-catching. Konstantinos Tzolakis, Tim Iroegbunam and Nobel Mendy all arrived in £20m-plus deals, while striker Robinio Vaz looks to be a potentially exciting deadline day addition on loan from Roma.

Now it’s on Sergej Jakirovic to put the pieces of the puzzle together.

View 13 Images (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ipswich Town: B

If the Tractor Boys are going to stay up, they’re probably going to have to do so with the “we’ll score one more than you” mentality. The signings of Julio Enciso, Emersonn, Daizen Maeda, Zian Flemming and Abdul Fatawu give Gary O’Neil plenty to work with in attack.

The question is can their defence handle the onslaught they’re going to face between now and May? They might well end up regretting the top-heavy recruitment.

Leeds United: A-

James Trafford gives Leeds a long-term No.1 with serious pedigree, Tarik Muharemovic was an ambitious defensive addition and Nico Elvedi brings experience at a low cost. Harry Wilson may also prove to be one of the smarter free transfers of the window, while Jean-Matteo Bahoya and Melvin Bard provide additional options without forcing Leeds into major permanent spending.

Pascal Struijk is the biggest loss, while Wilfried Gnonto and Joel Piroe have gone on loan and several goalkeepers have been moved out as that department was reshaped. Leeds have on the whole replaced what they lost with younger or higher-ceiling alternatives and addressed obvious weaknesses.

‌



View 13 Images (Image: Lee Keuneke/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Liverpool: B-

View 13 Images Liverpool landed Bradley Barcola after a long transfer saga (Image: Getty )

The priority at Liverpool was clearly to bolster their defence and options on the wing this summer. They tried to address the former by bringing in the experienced Ronald Araujo on loan, but it remains to be seen whether the Uruguayan and Jeremy Jacquet can convincingly fill Ibrahima Konate’s shoes at centre-back. Andoni Iraola’s lack of options at full-back are also concerning, given Conor Bradley’s injury and Andy Robertson leaving on a free transfer.

On a positive note, Bradley Barcola is a blockbuster acquisition who immediately gives Liverpool a new elite threat from the left, while Victor Munoz adds further attacking talent. But, for all the money spent by the Reds, there are still questions over the balance of the midfield.

‌



Manchester City: A-

It seems as if Manchester City somehow manage to undergo a squad rebuild every transfer window. The departure of Rodri was a huge loss, but City responded as best as they possibly could, adding £125m star Enzo Fernandez, £116m Elliot Anderson and £86m Ayyoub Bouaddi to bolster Enzo Maresca’s options. Iliman Ndiaye’s late addition hands the Etihad side another talented forward and Allan Elias adds further potential, making it difficult to criticise City’s window.

Meanwhile, Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez, Savio, John Stones, Bernardo Silva, Nathan Ake and Manuel Akanji have all departed, either permanently or on loan. City raised huge money and refreshed an ageing group in one attempt, showing they are still England’s most capable club when it comes to transfers.

Manchester United: B-

New signings Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans transformed the profile of a midfield which desperately needed more athleticism, physicality and control. All three are worthy of starting and Baleba in particular addresses a problem Manchester United have carried for several seasons. Yet, failing to add the left-back they were looking for leaves a glaring hole in the squad.

Rasmus Hojlund’s sale and Casemiro’s departure continued the rebuild, while Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir were moved out on loan. Jadon Sancho and Tyrell Malacia finally left at the end of their contracts. There has been a useful removal of deadwood and the midfield is undeniably better, but no back-up striker and no new left-back means United ended another expensive window with two obvious jobs unfinished.

‌



View 13 Images Carlos Baleba moved to Man Utd for £70m (Image: Getty Images)

Newcastle: B-

"It ain't about how hard you hit. It's about how hard you can get hit and keep moving forward." - Rocky Balboa, 2006. Newcastle looked like they’d gone 12 rounds in a 2v1 handicap bout against Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua after losing Gordon, Tonali, Bruno and Eddie Howe. Not a bad idea that actually, someone get Eddie Hearn on the phone.

Nico Gonzalez looked a great like-for-like Tonali replacement in the win at Spurs last weekend. Matias Fernandez-Pardo could prove to be quite the coup in time and Lukas Hornicek appears to be the upgrade needed on Nick Pope. A total outlay of £300m is quite the haymaker response.

But mass exoduses rarely do turn out as bad as first feared. Recruitment continues to be forward-thinking at St James’ and Matthias Jaissle now has a hungry bunch of players who want to play for the club, which goes a long way. A rebuild takes time, so the Geordies are going to have to be patient.

‌



View 13 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Nottingham Forest: B

Oliver Glasner wanted to be properly backed in the transfer market for a change. Just his luck that Forest decided not to reach double figures of signings for the first time in years!

Joking aside, they’ve done some smart business, reuniting Glasner with some of his favourites and avoiding any further notable exits after Elliot Anderson. Went about their business quietly.

The verdict's out on Liam Delap, especially at £45m, but if anyone can get him firing again it's Glasner. He's been reunited with old favourites Daniel Munoz and Xaver Schlager. Forest have a knack when it comes to rock-solid centre-backs and Ousmane Diomande looks the part.

‌



View 13 Images (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Sunderland: C+

Second season syndrome can be a cripping condition at the best of times, let alone when you’ve got Thursday night football on the agenda too. If Sunderland wanted to continue progressing, they needed a window like they had 12 months ago. They didn’t.

Regis Le Bris will have to pick his battles and play his cards smartly this season. They’ve done well, just not well enough for the position they find themselves in - and that’s to their credit after going above and beyond expectations.

Beating Arsenal and Palace to the buzzer-beater £30m signing of Malick Fofana was quite the statement. Thomas Meunier on a free is savvy business and Kevin Danso reinforces an already assured backline.

‌



Tottenham: B+

It is the history of the Tottenham, Giorgio Chiellini once wisely said. Even after breaking their transfer record twice for two of the Premier League’s best midfielders in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, and snapping up some savvy free signings early doors with Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, they still had the trademark Spursy finish to the window.

From competing with Man City for Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye to signing their outcasts and loaning Mykhailo Mudryk, who was linked with *checks notes* Coventry and Chelsea B, aka Strasbourg. Deary me. A combined £135m on Savio and Omar Marmoush, once the latter's obligation to buy is activated, feels very steep, as did the £52m on Jan Paul van Hecke.

Spurs can, however, say they’ve backed a manager for a change, so Roberto De Zerbi has no excuses.

Sports.title: Liverpool made Monaco call to make plan clear as Chelsea's Lamine Camara transfer collapsed
Sports.content:
Liverpool made Monaco call to make plan clear as Chelsea's Lamine Camara transfer collapsed

Chelsea missed out on landing Monaco's Lamine Camara late on deadline day - but Liverpool have told the French side they're keen on landing the midfielder next summer

View 2 Images Lamine Camara was close to a move to Chelsea (Image: Jan Kruger, Getty Images)

Chelsea's move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara failed to materialise late in the day - with Liverpool putting a call into the French side to express their interest in a future transfer.

‌



The Blues found themselves seeking a new midfielder on deadline day after it became apparent that Enzo Fernandez was bound for Manchester City. After having two bids turned down by the French outfit, Chelsea eventually secured a breakthrough and were closing in on the £47.1million signing of Camara, before the plug was pulled at the eleventh hour.

‌



TalkSport reports that Monaco still believe they can demand top dollar for their midfielder and Liverpool made contact to let the Ligue 1 club know that they would be keen to sign him in the future, potentially next summer. Liverpool's call had no bearing on Chelsea's move not coming to fruition.

‌



Monaco are ready to hold out for £60m and the Reds' midfield is an area that could be exposed this season, which would prompt action in the transfer market.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chelsea were left fuming by the collapse of the deal with Xabi Alonso now lacking a body in midfield, even if Fernandez had largely been shunned to begin the season, owing to the noise that was surrounding his future.

‌



Roma's Manu Kone was another midfielder high on Chelsea's wishlist but they failed to land the Frenchman, who impressed at the World Cup. They were close to an agreement to sign Kone, but Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini was determined to keep hold of the player, according to Sky in Italy.

So far this season Romeo Lavia, who has been plagued by injury issues, has started both Premier League games for Chelsea in midfield and been paired with Reece James and Cole Palmer as the Blues adapt to the new system employed by Alonso.

View 2 Images Liverpool have informed Monaco of their future interest in their midfielder (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



Another of Monaco's potential outings also fell through when Folarin Balogun, who was close to joining Everton, opted against the move. After initial concerns were raised during Balogun’s medical the player himself decided not to go ahead with the move to Merseyside.

Monaco have ultimately shown themselves willing to cash in on their top assets if the price is right. Kylian Mbappe remains the biggest departure of the last decade but since him the likes of Aurelien Tchouameni head to Real Madrid whilst this summer Maghnes Akliouche headed to PSG.

Sports.title: Carse left out of England squad for third Pakistan Test
Sports.content:
Brydon Carse and Matthew Fisher have both been left out of England's 15-man squad for the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

England are chasing a 3-0 series sweep, live from September 9-13 on Sky Sports, having thrashed the tourists by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley before claiming a 194-run victory at Lord's.

Carse was withdrawn from the squad for the second Test, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an incident that saw the Durham player briefly arrested outside a Derby nightclub on August 22.

Image: Brydon Carse has been left out England's squad for the third Test

Derbyshire Police are looking into "allegations of assault" against the 31-year-old, with right-armer Sonny Baker retaining his place in Joe Root's squad as Carse's replacement, while Fisher misses out after being unused in the first two Tests.

Carse was also left out of Durham's squad for their County Championship match against Northamptonshire, which began on Wednesday, due to 'pre-arranged workload management", despite finishing with match figures of 4-95 in their previous win over Gloucestershire.

Image: Carse featured in the County Championship for Durham last week

Speaking at Lord's last week, England captain Joe Root described himself as "hacked off" by the growing number of alcohol-related stories around the team, adding: "I've spoken to Brydon and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gave his reaction to the latest incident involving an England player at a nightclub, after video footage emerged of Brydon Carse in handcuffs on Saturday night

England's interim head coach Marcus Trescothick has indicated a preference to field his strongest possible side in pursuit of a 3-0 scoreline, rather than ring the changes.

That means Baker and Sam Cook may be kept on the sidelines, unless it is decided that any of the in-form pace attack of Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Atkinson need to be rested.

An inexperienced Pakistan outfit have been skittled for under 200 in all four innings so far, only batting beyond 50 overs once, with the relentless accuracy of Robinson - who finished with match figures of 8-35 in the second Test, backed up brilliantly by England's other seamers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Player of the second Test, Ollie Robinson, spoke glowingly about England's bowling attack and new-ball partner Jofra Archer

England squad: Joe Root (Yorkshire, captain), Jofra Archer (Sussex), Gus Atkinson (Surrey), Sonny Baker (Hampshire), Shoaib Bashir (Derbyshire), Harry Brook (Yorkshire), Sam Cook (Essex), Jordan Cox (Essex), Ben Duckett (Nottinghamshire), Emilio Gay (Durham), Dan Lawrence (Surrey), Ollie Pope (Surrey), Ollie Robinson (Sussex), Jamie Smith (Surrey), Josh Tongue (Nottinghamshire)

Pakistan make wholesale changes for Test dead rubber

Pakistan have dropped seven players and two coaches from their touring squad following their series defeat to England and ahead of the final Test at Edgbaston.

Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq - injured during the second Test defeat at Lord's - Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad have all been sent home.

Seven replacements have been called up to the squad, including five uncapped players at Test level, with batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal having eight and two Test appearances, respectively.

Sports.title: Why Balogun's move collapsed to leave Everton, Chelsea and Monaco upset
Sports.content:
The biggest controversy of the summer transfer window happened on Deadline Day, involving three clubs and two players.

Chelsea, Everton and Monaco ended up very frustrated as Folarin Balogun opted against joining Everton at the last minute after Monaco had earlier pulled out of a deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea, who wanted the midfielder as their Enzo Fernandez replacement.

The two Premier League sides were particularly left fuming about the situation.

Here, Sky Sports News takes you inside why both deals collapsed on a dramatic end to Deadline Day…

Everton uncover Balogun medical issue

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett explains why the collapse of the Folarin Balogun deal leaves Everton short of strikers

Monaco needed to make a sale to help resolve a debt issue, while Everton needed a striker.

Balogun became a solution for both parties, and a £40m agreement was reached - but then came the first issue with the deal.

There was a problem with the USA international's medical after Everton found evidence of an injury, which Monaco and the player refuted, claiming he was fit to play immediately.

With the 11pm deadline approaching, Everton decided to proceed with the transfer but attempted to renegotiate the deal on cheaper terms in case the injury left him unable to play.

The club-to-club deal became much more performance-related, with clauses inserted that meant Monaco would get less money if Balogun could not play.

Crucially, it is understood nothing changed with Balogun's personal terms.

How Everton's Zirkzee move angers Balogun

Image: Balogun (left) was unhappy over Everton's move for Man Utd's Joshua Zirkzee

Amid a renegotiation of the Balogun deal, Chelsea reached an agreement with Monaco to sign midfielder Camara as a replacement for Fernandez, who was set to join Manchester City in a joint-British record £125m deal.

Meanwhile, Everton made a loan offer for Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee, which was rejected.

Sky Sports News understands Everton offered to pay a total fee of around £10m for Zirkzee, which included his wages for the season and a loan fee.

But the feeling at Old Trafford was that Everton's approach came too late and was not of value.

The Toffees' pursuit of Zirkzee is what upset Balogun, who felt the club were going behind his back to sign someone else.

Balogun's unhappiness with Everton was revealed by Monaco chief Thiago Scuro at a press conference on Wednesday.

He said: "Balogun's allegation is that I'm not feeling well because of the way the club treated me.

"I'm not feeling well because Everton's medical department brought doubts about my future or my health.

"I have nothing (no medical problem), so I'm not comfortable to sign a long contract here."

Everton are understood to be surprised at the allegation that Balogun was made to feel unwanted, given they never renegotiated his personal terms and clearly wanted to get the deal done.

The renegotiation of the guaranteed fee payable to Monaco justified the risk given the issue with the medical.

Sky Sports News also understands that Everton's interest in Zirkzee was separate from the Balogun deal, with the club prepared to sign both players.

Everton feel the ex-Arsenal forward misunderstood their Zirkzee approach - they were not turning their attention to a different player.

Balogun's U-turn leaves everyone upset

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to Man City despite their Lamine Camara deal collapsing

Believing Balogun would be joining Everton, Monaco pulled the plug on Chelsea's deal for Camara.

The Ligue 1 side preferred selling Balogun over Camara because they only needed the money from one player sale.

But Balogun then sensationally decided to walk away from his Everton move over what he perceived as poor treatment from the Merseysiders.

His dramatic decision, which saw him miss out on his dream Premier League move, meant all three clubs were left disappointed.

Monaco kept both Balogun and Camara, failing to raise the money they wanted.

Everton missed out on signing a striker, leaving them with just one recognised striker, Thierno Barry, in their squad after selling Beto to Fiorentina in a £15.4m Deadline Day deal.

And Chelsea were left with no Fernandez replacement after he joined Man City - a deal which the Blues could have pulled out of but honoured despite having no replacement.

The question now is whether these deals could be revived in January? Well, you would say it is unlikely after this shambles.

Sports.title: Norris launches single-seater team LN4 Fusion ahead of 2027 debut
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has launched a new junior single-seater team, LN4 Fusion, which will race in multiple championships in 2027.

LN4 Fusion has acquired selected assets of Formula 3 team AIX Racing to race in the championship next year and is undertaking the relevant application procedure to compete in Formula 2 in the future.

The group, developed by a high-profile investment group led by Dan Richards, will also have teams in Italian F4 and Formula Regional in 2027 with plans to enter British F4 in the future

"I'm very excited. This is one of my biggest things I've ever been part of that's not just within my own stuff of Formula 1. Norris told Sky Sports F1 ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

"[It's] my very own race team that I co-founded. So I'll be having my own race team in all the junior series.

"Obviously, we want it to be the best. We want it to be the leading single-seater race team. But it's just very cool to be part of something new, create something, and for me to be part of something for such a long period of time as well."

Image: LN4 Fusion will compete in Formula 3 next year - one of Formula 1's support series (Image: LN4 Fusion)

Alongside LN4 Fusion, Norris is also launching the LN4 Legacy Programme - an independent, fully funded driver development programme, operated by ADD Management and led by experienced programme director Julian Rouse.

The programme aims to identify and support future talent for those who do not have the finances to move up the motorsport ladder.

"The main objective of this is simply to help younger drivers who have talent and have the ability to get to Formula 1, but probably not financially [the ability], and help them in all those other areas reach their end goal," said Norris.

"Basically my little way of trying to give back, again, using my team, using the people that I'm with, my partners, and give other people, give young drivers a chance. So that's my more personal side of things, which is pretty cool too."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris sits down with Sky Sports' Rob Jones to discuss extending his stay with McLaren in a multi-year contract extension

LN4 Fusion's principal European headquarters will be based in Veneto in Italy where a new facility is being built with a British operation in Cambridgeshire.

Norris added: "I was very lucky growing up that my dad could support me all the way through to Formula 2.

"But I know that there are a lot of other drivers out there who probably can get to Formula 1, but don't have the financial backing or the ability to know how to go through the whole programme, which is where the team comes into place too.

"This is my way, and we're talking hundreds of thousands, we're talking millions, in fact, of how I can bring my whole infrastructure together, my support, my knowledge, and try to give as many other people and certain other drivers opportunities to reach their goal too."
