Sports.title: Championship club rip up captain’s contract less than 24 hours after transfer window shuts
Sports.content:
Championship club rip up captain’s contract less than 24 hours after transfer window shuts

Charlton Athletic have confirmed that Greg Docherty has left the club after the transfer window closed.

The midfielder was the club captain, but he has left The Valley and is free to find another club.

2 Nathan Jones' side have made a brilliant start to the season, winning every league match Credit: Getty

The 29-year-old failed to appear in any of Charlton's opening Championship games.

And his game time was likely to further reduce due to the Addicks signing Oliver Skipp on loan.

Skipp completed a very late loan switch to Charlton from Leicester City on deadline day, and Docherty has now been released.

And in an emotional goodbye, the former skipper said: "To be named captain of such an iconic football club was nothing short of a privilege. I felt the weight and expectation that title carries, but I can wholeheartedly say I gave my absolute all to represent the club properly every single day with the upmost respect that I felt it deserved through the good and the bad moments.

"I joined the club with one aim: to help make Charlton an established Championship club again. Being the first captain to lead the club to promotion and then safety the following season is an achievement I am, and always will be, immensely proud of.

"Thinking back to the play-off campaign fills me with so much pride. From the first-leg pitch invasion at full time, to seeing 40,000+ red flags and shirts at Wembley and lifting the play-off final trophy, it’s a feeling I don’t think will ever be replicated.

"It goes without saying that I am devastated to be leaving this club but football moves fast. I’m so proud of what I achieved here and I leave behind an amazing chapter in my football career, an incredible group of teammates, staff and people behind the scenes who make this club what it is, along with genuine friendships that I’ll cherish for a long time.

"I’ll always be grateful for my time at Charlton and everything the club has given me, but football moves fast I’m now excited to see what the future holds.

"Thank you for all of your support. It’s been a pleasure."

In total, the Scotsman made 90 appearances for Charlton, joining the club from Hull City in the summer of 2024 for nothing and departs having helped Charlton to promotion to the Championship in his debut season.

2 Docherty became a modern day cult hero at The Valley Credit: Getty

One in, one out

The reason Docherty has been released is largely due to the arrival of Skipp.

The former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder has joined the Addicks on loan for the remainder of the season.

Skipp had played a couple of League One games, but he's now got a chance to impress in the Championship, and Nathan Jones is happy he's in the building.

Speaking to the club's website, Jones said: "We’re delighted to add Oliver to the squad. Skippy is someone that I’ve known for a long, long time. He’s got top-end Championship experience and Premier League experience.

"As soon as I spoke to him, he had a real desire to play for our club and be part of our project. He’s a player with wonderful experience, with wonderful quality.

"He’s a real marquee signing for us. It’s the culmination of a long, difficult and testing window, but one we’ve come through with a considerably improved squad.

"We have a really competitive Championship squad and I’m excited when we get everyone back, with what we can achieve."

Sports.title: KSI claims Dagenham & Redbridge is his ‘everything’ as he opens up on Premier League dream
Sports.content:
KSI claims Dagenham & Redbridge is his ‘everything’ as he opens up on Premier League dream

KSI has brought more eyes to Dagenham & Redbridge than the club has ever seen - now he wants to help them reach the Premier League.

The 33-year-old is into his first full season as a minority shareholder of the Daggers, who currently sit atop the National League South.

4 KSI is helping to usher in a new era at Dagenham and Redbridge Credit: Getty

The YouTuber, real name Olajide 'JJ' Olatunji, made national headlines when he invested in the sixth-tier outfit earlier this year.

KSI 'loving it' at Dagenham & Redbridge

Dagenham & Redbridge have since signed over 14 players on free transfers this summer, including Antony Papadopoulos from EFL side Crawley Town, who are two leagues above them.

And the KSI-effect has also paid dividends on the pitch, with his side two points clear in the National League South after six games.

"I'm loving it," the Londoner told talkSPORT's Ian Abrahams following Dagenham & Redbridge's 1-0 win over Slough Town. "It's fantastic.

"It's definitely a roller coaster. It's not easy.

"There are games where I'm thinking 'Yeah, Slough Town, [we] should easily destroy them 3-0', and we struggle at times just because we haven't been clinical enough.

"[Harry] Beautyman had several chances to just put this game to bed, and we didn't. And then a silly red card.

"Silly red card that we just don't need; Too many. I mean, we had what, three red cards in six games? It's not good.

"We need to improve discipline."

4 KSI has also filmed viral content with Andy Carroll, who doubles up as Dagenham's striker and assistant manager Credit: Getty

Why KSI invested in Dagenham & Redbridge

Since his initial investment, the influencer has since been joined in Dagenham by former Queens Park Rangers owner Tony Fernandes.

The Malaysian businessman, who was a shareholder at QPR between 2011 and 2023, bought a 40 per cent stake in the east London club.

Asked whether his decision to enter the game was a result of either his inability to be a professional footballer or his desire to see Dagenham & Redbridge flourish further up the English pyramid, KSI replied: "It's the second option because, for me, like I have joy in seeing others win and this is my club, man.

"I want it to reach the highest of highs. I've set a goal: Premier League." By? "No, I'm not gonna say..." KSI continued.

"It's football; anything can happen, but that's my goal, and I want to see this club in the Premier League with the best."

4 KSI live streams matches as part of an agreement with DAZN Credit: Getty

'I've brought more eyes than Dagenham and Redbridge has ever really seen'

KSI boasts over 46 million subscribers across his four active YouTube channels and is the co-owner of several businesses as well.

He is the co-founder of Misfits Boxing and has also served as a judge on Britain's Got Talent in recent years.

But already in his work at the Daggers, KSI has agreed a unique broadcasting deal with DAZN to live stream a number of the club's fixtures on YouTube throughout the season.

"My expertise are marketing and media," He told talkSPORT. "Getting eyes on the club, and that's what I'm doing.

"Every game I come, every time I'm posting about Dagenham & Redbridge, it's just one new fan that's checking them out and joining the journey.

"So for me, I've brought more eyes than Dagenham and Redbridge has ever really seen. So we just need to keep it up."

"It already has [taken over my life] - This is everything for me. This is everything; whenever I go and do something, I'm all in. With Daggers, I'm all in, with all the publicity that I'm giving it.

4 KSI hopes to one day bring Premier League football to Victoria Road Credit: Rex

"I just want Dagenham and Redbridge to perform at the highest level. I want all the fans to be supporting.

"I want them to love this club. I want them to come to games and just be obsessed with everything.

Every time we've been at home, the atmosphere's been great. I was with the ultras today, and it was great, man.

"I loved it; Like the energy. They're all standing up the whole time. I was just fully giving it, chances left, right and centre.

"It was a great time, and people watching the stream will look at it, and go, 'You know what? This looks jokes. I want to be a part of this.'

"So yeah, that's the goal. I want people to just come here, enjoy it and join the journey."

Sports.title: Monaco CEO comes out swinging in fiery press conference over Chelsea and Everton transfer chaos
Sports.content:
Monaco CEO comes out swinging in fiery press conference over Chelsea and Everton transfer chaos

Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro has explained why Lamine Camara and Folarin Balogun's Premier League transfers fell through.

Camara and Balogun were on the brink of joining Chelsea and Everton respectively, but saw their deals collapse.

5 Scuro held a fiery press conference on Wednesday, explaining why the deals collapsed Credit: AFP

In Camara's case, it was Monaco who pulled the plug on the move in the final moments on Deadline Day on Tuesday night.

The midfielder had said yes to a six-year contract at Stamford Bridge after a £47million deal had been agreed with Chelsea.

However, the Ligue 1 side opted not to sell him right before the deadline, leaving the Blues furious with their decision.

A club source told talkSPORT: "Monaco have acted in a deeply unprofessional way."

And as for Balogun, his transfer to Everton fell through in the last few moments of the summer window too.

But in his case, it was his decision to back out and return to France after a significant issue was found in his medical.

Monaco agreed to change terms with the Toffees following his medical, but Balogun didn't want to join in the end.

The transfer chaos led to backlash coming Monaco's way, so CEO Scuro called a press conference on Wednesday to defend the club and explain why the deals didn't work out.

Why did Camara and Balogun's transfers fall through?

"During the day, we had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton," Scuro explained. "Balogun flew yesterday morning to go for medicals and sign a contract.

"Balogun, besides the salary, was also an important source of income for the club, which would help us also to balance the season. And then, Lamine [was] staying.

5 Balogun was in Liverpool completing his medical on Deadline Day before the deal broke down Credit: Getty

"This was what we had until mid-afternoon. What happened is that Chelsea was always testing and trying. What about Lamine? What about Lamine? I’ve been talking to them for the last ten days.

"Around 4pm yesterday, we got a contact from Chelsea. Okay, we sold a player in this position (Enzo Fernandez). Deal done. Is there any possibility that Monaco is open to selling Lamine?

"The answer was the same. No, it’s not. At this moment, at 4pm Balogun was in Liverpool undergoing his medical. Everything was going pretty well.

"Around 7pm, we were contacted by Everton, raising questions about Balogun’s medical, which, for our medical staff, as well as for the player’s personal medical staff, made no sense at all.

"The explanations were not enough to justify or to bring concerns regarding the future of the player, which there aren’t. This discussion started between medical departments from here and there."

Scuro then said that Everton spent multiple hours doing a 'deep assessment' and checking with other doctors regarding Balogun's fitness following the medical.

5 Negotiations for Camara began with Chelsea as Balogun's move looked to be stalling Credit: Getty

And as that was happening, the news broke in the media that some issues had arisen and that Balogun may not join Everton.

Scuro continued: "Of course, Chelsea saw the opportunity. ‘OK, Monaco needs money. Balogun is struggling there. Let’s go. Let’s try.’ And this is the game. It’s fair to play this game. There is no problem.

"Chelsea came and called us. Oh, maybe I can be here for the solution. And at that moment, we had to open the door for the discussion.

"This was almost 8pm. We started negotiations with Chelsea. I informed the player directly myself. I called him. I informed his agent, as we always do. Very open. We had discussions about the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea.

"At the same time, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balogun. And what happened was that around 10pm, in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that, OK, there is no problem. We are ready to do it. Let’s sign the contract.

"As soon as we got the information, we came back to Chelsea and thought, OK, we have our deal there. There is no deal on [Camara]. Because it’s also fair to do this. It’s also part of the game.

5 A deal sheet was submitted for Balogun but he then decided to pull out of the transfer Credit: AFP

"There is no reason that these kinds of discussions are dynamic on the last day of the transfer window, which all of us decided to be on the last day, trying to find solutions, with the clock ticking, that now this kind of interaction [sees us] become the bad guys in the room.

"That Monaco is ‘not fair, Monaco is not right. Everybody is very fair and nice in the football industry. Just Monaco is not.’ Too much.

Scuro concluded: "We informed, again, everyone that there was no deal with Chelsea. We progressed. The Premier League has a mechanism in which you can request one extra hour to finish the paperwork. This was done.

"Five minutes to close the transfer window there, for us to finish all the paperwork between Monaco and Everton and Balo. I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract. At the last moment, the players decided not to sign.

"And basically, Balogun’s allegation is that I’m not feeling well because of the way the club treated me. I’m not feeling well because Everton’s medical department raised doubts about my future or my health. I have nothing, so I’m not comfortable signing a long contract here.

"And that’s the way we finish our transfer window."

5 Camara wanted to join Chelsea but amid the chaos, Monaco ended up keeping him

How are Balogun and Camara feeling?

Scuro went on to provide some detail on how the two Monaco stars are feeling after their transfer drama on Deadline Day.

He said: "For Balogun, I only spoke to him by phone. His arguments are clear. He’s coming back. I think he took the decision. There is not a big reason for him to be affected too much because it’s his decision.

"On Lamine, I really respect and understand. Because the player might have got excited yesterday during the day by conversations with the coach... by everything that a club like Chelsea can propose and promise to a player.

"At the end of the day, he also asked us to try to find a solution for him to leave. But again, we explained the reasons why we did what we did.

"And now we’re going to keep respecting and working with him. Knowing his mentality and his character, we can expect him full power in the next game. He’s going to keep building his career.

"As with many other players, better things will come in the future. This is not the end of the world. It’s just one possibility for a player on his level with his talent. I’m very confident that soon he will have even better options and offers than the one he had yesterday."

Sports.title: Ipswich vs Liverpool LIVE commentary: Bradley Barcola in line for debut as Reds chase first win
Sports.content:
Ipswich vs Liverpool LIVE commentary: Bradley Barcola in line for debut as Reds chase first win

Liverpool travel to Ipswich in the Premier League on Friday evening chasing their first win of the season, live on talkSPORT.

The Reds under Andoni Iraola have drawn their opening two games 2-2 against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

4 Gary O'Neil oversaw a 2-1 win over Sunderland in his first game as Ipswich manager Credit: Getty

4 Andoni Iraola is still looking for his first victory as Liverpool head coach Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, the newly promoted Tractor Boys kicked off by beating Sunderland but were thrashed 5-2 by Manchester United last time out.

It's a repeat of Ipswich's first game of the 2024/25 campaign – when they returned to the Premier League after 22 years away and were beaten 2-0 by Liverpool in their first outing under Arne Slot, who went on to lead them to the title.

Both sides made big signings late in the transfer window, with Liverpool finally securing the services of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain while Ipswich landed striker Zian Flemming from Burnley.

How to follow Ipswich vs Liverpool

This clash, the first Premier League fixture of Matchweek 3, takes place on Friday, September 4.

Kick-off at Portman Road is at 8pm.

talkSPORT's exclusive live radio coverage of the match will be hosted by Hugh Woozencroft.

Commentary comes from Jim Proudfoot and former West Ham and England striker Dean Ashton.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

4 Barcola could make his first club appearance since winning the Champions League final with PSG in May Credit: Getty

Ipswich vs Liverpool team news

Both sides are without a number of players for this encounter due to injury.

Ipswich are still missing two of their promotion winners, Jack Taylor and Jaden Philogene-Bidace, neither of whom has featured in a matchday squad so far in 2026/27.

They'll also be hoping the issue that forced their club-record signing, striker Emersonn, off at half-time of the defeat to Man United isn't anything serious.

As for Liverpool, Hugo Ekitike is expected to be sidelined until the New Year as he continues his recovery from the ruptured Achilles he sustained in April.

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni, both long-term absentees with knee injuries, are closing in on a return but won't be fit for the trip to Suffolk.

Of the aforementioned new arrivals, Flemming seems the more likely to start having already featured heavily for Burnley in the Championship this season.

It might well be a case of introducing Barcola from the bench given that he hasn't played any competitive football since the World Cup, where he helped France to a fourth-placed finish.

4 Flemming could make his Ipswich debut after scoring three goals already for Burnley this campaign Credit: Getty

Iraola growing frustrated

Reflecting on his team's loss to United, O'Neil said Ipswich need to 'handle the momentum' better and keep on top of their 'emotional discipline'.

He added: "We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us.

"It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don't want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand."

Iraola was left 'frustrated' at failing to beat Forest, though he praised Liverpool's second-half performance in a match in which they twice came from behind to clinch a point.

He said "I'm frustrated because we want to win - especially at home. It's not a good result to draw at home.

"It's true that we've come back from two results where we were losing, like the other day against Newcastle. But at the end what makes the difference are the wins and the three points.

"I like what we've done in the second half, but we haven't been able to complete the comeback and the point. It leaves you frustrated, yes."

Sports.title: How Newcastle's transfer window went from bruising to brilliant: 'F***ing Liverpool', David Hopkinson's secret trip to Lille, Ross Wilson's flight diversion fortune, why Matthias Jaissle wanted Amar Dedic and why they walked away from James Trafford
Sports.content:
Ripping off the sticking plaster. That is how insiders have described the decision to sell Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. With hindsight, the strategy makes sense. There was a point this summer, however, when Newcastle United were bleeding.

Take June 17. Club doctor Paul Catterson had flown to the United States, ready to complete the medical of Spain’s World Cup winger Victor Munoz. Then, the messages started circulating. ‘F***ing Liverpool’. The Reds had hijacked the deal.

It was a bruising start. Come July 13, the black and whites were well and truly black and blue. Recruitment staff had been back and forth to North America and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, a breakout star at the World Cup, had been presented with Newcastle’s vision for him.

Chief executive David Hopkinson met the 20-year-old’s family. After the disappointment of Munoz, this was a goer. And then it was gone. Manzambi chose Aston Villa at the 11th hour.

Both deals had been played out in public. There was a need for stealth. Sporting director Ross Wilson flew to Germany to close a deal for Hoffenheim winger Bazoumana Toure. He had got in, and out, unnoticed.

But then, his flight back to Newcastle from Frankfurt was diverted to Paris. In a Charles de Gaulle departure lounge, a Newcastle fan spotted him. Wilson was grilled about signing a player from France. The cover story suited him fine. It was a brief moment of levity amid the turbulence of June.

Newcastle United sporting director Ross Wilson (left) and the club's chief executive David Hopkinson have had a busy summer but can be pleased with their transfer dealings

Amar Dedic, a £30m right back from Benfica, was a player already on Newcastle's radar but was then pursued on the say-so of new manager Matthias Jaissle

All the while, Guimaraes had instructed super agents to find him a new club. Newcastle had known this for several weeks and it was only when Daily Mail Sport broke the story of talks with Arsenal on June 25 that the reality was known to the rest of the world.

The night before, Eddie Howe sat in the Miami Stadium and watched his captain play for Brazil. The desire was to keep him, but Guimaraes had let it be known he was determined to go.

The narrative was set – Newcastle were losing their best players and losing their replacements. Then, on the eve of pre-season, they lost Howe. The head coach told Wilson he was standing down but agreed to stay on until his successor was found. Gordon had already joined Barcelona and Tonali was on his way to Tottenham.

Mess. Calamity. Car crash. Call it what you like – and we all did – this had the makings of a summer to rival the disaster of 12 months previous, the wreckage of which Newcastle were still clearing.

That unease outstayed the appointment of Matthias Jaissle and even the final pre-season friendly. New recruits Toure and Aladji Bamba – two 20-year-olds at a combined £72.5m – did not look ready to start in the Premier League.

There were holes in the squad and the XI. Jaissle referenced a ‘leadership void’. Privately and publicly, he made clear the need for signings.

The headlines were noted inside St James’ Park. Were Newcastle relegation candidates? The question was asked by outsiders and it was not unreasonable. Those on the inside kept their counsel and, crucially, their nerve.

Just over a fortnight later and here we are, with Newcastle in the conversation as transfer-window winners. It helps that Guimaraes started the season injured at Arsenal, and that Tonali, despite playing, has barely started the season at all at Spurs.

The desire was to keep Bruno Guimaraes but the Brazilian had let it be known he was determined to go, which added to the early window turmoil

The £50m midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who joined last week from Manchester City, was superb in the win at Tottenham

It helps far more that the players brought in have hit the ground running. And passing. And crossing. And creating.

Amar Dedic, a £30m right back from Benfica, was a player already on the radar but then pursued on the say-so of Jaissle, who worked with him at RB Salzburg. He arrived five days before the start of the season. With three assists from two games and a robust style that lends itself to attack and defence, the Bosnian will already have rival recruitment departments wondering how they missed him.

Alongside Dedic, £50m midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who joined last week, and £26m goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek were Newcastle’s best players during Saturday’s 2-0 win at Tottenham. Sean Steur, a cultured 18-year-old midfielder from Ajax, looks a steal at £20m. From the darkness of pre-season has come the light of the campaign proper.

There was, before Spurs, a draw against Liverpool from which Newcastle deserved more. There was also the announcement of a new £190m training-ground development. And then Jaissle, a manager who has exuded energy, intelligence and belief, not least in himself.

Wilson and senior staff knew that the optics had changed – getting Gonzalez out of Manchester City for half of the £100m they received for Tonali felt like a major coup – and so they pushed ahead with one last ambitious move, for a player they had previously thought unattainable.

On Friday morning of last week, Wilson and Hopkinson took the Eurostar to Lille. There, they agreed a deal to sign Matias Fernandez-Pardo for £51m. The framework had been in place for several days.

When Wilson was then pictured walking into the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday afternoon, supporters online questioned why he was not elsewhere making transfers happen. The answer was in his inside pocket – his passport, freshly stamped from the return journey.

Over the weekend, he and Hopkinson waited nervously for the Ligue 1 side to find a replacement and, just as importantly, for the likes of Liverpool – yes, ‘f****** Liverpool’ – to stay away from the winger. Some of those around the 21-year-old also needed to be persuaded that Tyneside was the best destination for the Belgium international. It all felt very precarious.

On Friday morning of last week, Wilson and Hopkinson took the Eurostar to Lille. There, they agreed a deal to sign Matias Fernandez-Pardo for £51m

Sean Steur, a cultured 18-year-old midfielder from Ajax, looks a steal at £20m

Hopkinson remained in London on Sunday, a strategic ploy keeping him closer to northern France than North East England. On Monday morning, amber turned to green. By tea-time, Fernandez-Pardo was on a flight to Newcastle.

His deadline-day signing took the total to eight, at a cost of around £270m, making a net spend of just £25m. The Squad Cost Ratio deficit that resulted in a UEFA fine last season has been addressed, while the removal of Nick Woltemade’s wage, coupled with a £3.5m loan fee from Juventus, has all but covered the SCR cost of Fernandez-Pardo’s transfer fee for the first season.

In short, by playing the long game this summer, Newcastle insist they have left themselves in a much stronger position financially. Hopkinson’s mid-summer declaration of Newcastle 2.0 – post Howe and those departing stars – felt suspiciously like Newcastle 1.5 going into the new season.

But now, with the window closed and the view no longer blurred, the picture is one of positivity and prosperity. They have ridden misfortune and some misadventure, and those two have, on occasion, collided to more fortunate consequence.

Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, 31, pulling out a move from Marseille and Joao Palhinha, also 31, preferring a return to Portugal from Bayern Munich were soon followed by encouragement that a deal for Gonzalez, 24, was possible. Newcastle had dropped a penny and found a pound.

Of all the holding midfielders they sought, insiders believe Gonzalez represents the best outcome. Brighton’s Carlos Baleba briefly became a possibility last month when agents said he was available for around £65m – Jaissle was said to like the player – and Tottenham’s Lucas Bergvall and Archie Gray were discussed in and around the sale of Tonali. Former Forest midfielder Danilo was offered and considered, but Newcastle wanted better.

The framework of a deal for AC Milan’s Christopher Nkunku, 28, was agreed with the Italian club two weeks ago. Jaissle was aware of him through the Red Bull network – Nkunku scored 70 goals for RB Leipzig over four seasons – but Leipzig is where the forward wanted to return.

Out wide, Cologne’s Said El Mala was admired and tracked, while Zadok Yohanna, a 19-year-old of AIK, chose Brighton over Newcastle.

A £15m offer from Nottingham Forest for Jacob Murphy was rejected this week on the insistence of new boss Jaissle

Goalkeeper James Trafford was the No 1 target coming into the window, but his insistence that his future was only decided after the World Cup caused frustration

In defence, they liked Forest full back Neco Williams but he was not for sale. Giorgio Scalvini, the Atalanta centre back, was always on the list, but Newcastle decided to trust their current quartet in that position.

Goalkeeper James Trafford was the No 1 target coming into the window, but his insistence that his future was only decided after the World Cup, despite being England’s third-choice keeper, caused frustration. After failed moves for Trafford the previous two summers, Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek, who also had interest from Manchester City.

As for outgoings, a £15m offer from Forest for Jacob Murphy was rejected this week on the insistence of Jaissle. He sees the winger's value as a senior presence in a young dressing room and, despite the obvious SCR benefits of selling a 31-year-old in the final year of his contract, the manager got his way.

By this point, the club’s need to appease the balance sheet was far less than the need to appease their new boss on the back of his encouraging start.

The sticking plaster was ripped off for good reason. Supporters and observers spent much of the summer staring at the wound, but the bigger mistake was assuming it would never heal.

Sports.title: The great Ashes ticket rip-off: Execs defend 'disgraceful' decision to hike ticket prices for next summer's Ashes Tests - with top seats setting punters back £250
Sports.content:
The great Ashes ticket rip-off: Execs defend 'disgraceful' decision to hike ticket prices for next summer's Ashes Tests - with top seats setting punters back £250

Warwickshire are at the centre of an Ashes price storm after it was revealed that it will cost almost one and a half times as much to watch England take on Australia next year than it did in 2023.

The ballot for tickets across all five of the 2027 venues was opened simultaneously on Wednesday morning under direction from the ECB, triggering a mix of astonishment and anger from fans at Edgbaston’s prices.

Reacting on X, one user referred to the entry costs released to Warwickshire members as ‘eye watering’ while another dubbed them a ‘disgrace’.

Although members can purchase seats for £92, the cheapest adult admission elsewhere in the ground for the first three days of the July 8-12 match is £115 while one in the popular Eric Hollies Stand will set you back £165 - up 43% on the £115 for the corresponding fixture in 2023. Each ticket carries an additional £2.50 booking charge.

The most expensive in general admission can be found in Edgbaston’s City End Social, priced up at £250.

The equivalent City End purchase for next week’s Test match versus Pakistan - which includes access to the Xcelerate lounge, two free drinks of your choice and a folding seat in the RES Wyatt Stand - is £127.50.

Tickets in Edgbaston's Eric Hollies Stand will set you back £165 - up 43% on the £115 for the corresponding fixture in 2023

Defending the hike, an Edgbaston Stadium spokesperson said: ‘Our prices for the 2027 Ashes Test are broadly in line with other host venues and major British sporting events such as Wimbledon and the Formula One at Silverstone.

‘Our entry level ticket prices roughly match inflation compared to the last time Australia visited Edgbaston in 2023 - but like the rest of the country, we're battling increased costs and trying to manage these wherever we can.’

Edgbaston is still cheaper than the two London venues of Lord’s and The Oval, but the increase in turnstile tariffs is another blow to northern supporters whose nearest access to Test cricket next summer comes either in Birmingham or at Nottingham’s Trent Bridge.

Nottinghamshire have looked to reward loyalty by capping all members’ tickets at the Stuart Broad End, which provides pavilion access, at £90. Although purchases are limited to two each. The most affordable public entry is £99 for days one to three and £85 for day four while all fifth day tickets cost a flat rate of £40.

Perhaps surprisingly, the range at Lord’s from £125 to £195 - representing an increase from £115-190 in the 2023 Ashes - means the most expensive have gone up by less than 2.5%.

MCC, the ground’s owners, have also made restricted view tickets available at £100 and designated a higher proportion of Under-16 seats across all stands at the ground than they did three years ago for Australia’s last visit.

Lord’s Tests in the interim have attracted criticism for the quality of pitches produced, yet it has not impacted on demand, with more than one million applications made for major match day tickets in 2026.

And while pricing remains a thorny issue, one executive involved told Daily Mail Sport: ‘We could satisfy demand for Ashes tickets three times over, and that leaves us in a position whereby you are balancing the cost at the bottom end, making the match as accessible as possible to all, while not undermining the need to maximise income from what is arguably the biggest marquee event in world cricket.’

Across the Thames at The Oval, Surrey have kept in line with inflation, marking the most expensive seats at £185 while 1,000 tickets daily of their overall 27,500 capacity are at the entry level of £115. Their equivalents in 2023 were £105 and £165. Members get a discount.

Hampshire’s Utilita Bowl, making its Ashes debut next year, has a price e structure that begins at £95 for adults and £45 for Under-17s across the opening four days and drops to £35 and £10 respectively for people who want to gamble on there being a fifth.

Meanwhile, Warwickshire have struggled to sell tickets for next week’s dead rubber third Test between England and Pakistan, with around 12,000 apiece taken for days one and two. Confidence remains, however, that a reduced full house of 19,000 - Edgbaston is currently undergoing reconstruction work - will be in attendance for Friday’s third day.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods strikes deal and pleads guilty to reckless driving... after arriving at court with doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods has pleaded guilty to reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after striking a deal with prosecutors in the wake of his DUI arrest.

The golf legend was suited-and-booted as he arrived at court with girlfriend Vanessa Trump on his arm, looking stoic while wading through photographers outside the Martin County Court shortly after 8am on Wednesday.

Woods was pictured in the courtroom moments later, where he stood in front of a judge and changed his plea. He was originally charged with driving under the influence but has now pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of reckless driving.

As part of the deal, Woods will have his license suspended for five years.

The 15-time major champion was found at the scene of the crash in Jupiter, Florida, with two opioid tablets in his pocket, on March 27.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but had not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

Tiger Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving at a hearing in Florida on Wednesday morning

Woods appeared puffy-eyed as he left the court alongside doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump

Vanessa led him back to their car after he had pleaded guilty and had his license suspended

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

He was able to crawl out of the car without any injuries before later admitting to officers he was looking at his phone and changing the radio at the time of the collision.

A Breathalyzer test did not reveal any alcohol in Woods’s system, but he refused a urine test, according to police.

The Sheriff’s report obtained by the Daily Mail said deputies found opioids in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment.

A previous hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods's attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods appeared puffy-faced as he arrived for his change-of-plea hearing in Florida

Vanessa was front and center inside the court as Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods in the back of a police cruiser after being arrested on suspicion of DUI in March

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

He hasn't competed since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon in Scotland and has since undergone surgery to repair a torn Achilles as well as a seventh back procedure.

Woods' legal problems have since been put into perspective by Vanessa's cancer diagnosis. She revealed her bout with an unspecified form of breast cancer back in May.

The March crash marked the fourth major driving-related incident of Woods's adult life.

Five years earlier, when Woods rolled another SUV down a steep embankment in California, he did not face any accusations of driving under the influence. Instead, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department claimed Woods was driving at around 80mph, nearly twice the legal limit, at the time of the crash.

Witnesses told TMZ that Woods appeared agitated and impatient while leaving a golf tournament parking lot in the moments before the crash.

Woods after his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) in Jupiter, Florida, on May 29, 2017. He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods changed his original not guilty plea in the wake of his DUI arrest back in March

Vanessa with him and her 19-year-old daughter Kai back in March

Woods was never charged in 2021, but he wasn't so lucky in 2017, when he was found by Jupiter police about 15 miles from his home. Officers said they found him unconscious in his Mercedes-Benz, which was parked awkwardly on the roadside at around 3am.

Upon closer inspection, they noticed damage to his vehicle.

Woods didn't have any alcohol in his system, but later tests found the active ingredient for marijuana, two painkillers - Vicodin and Dilaudid - the sleep drug Ambien and the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

He later claimed he had been self-medicating for pain caused by his fourth back surgery and insomnia. Woods did not specifically address the marijuana issue and he wasn't found with the drug in his possession.

Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving and received a year of probation, a $250 fine and was ordered to undergo 50 hours of community service. He was also banned from drinking alcohol during the probation.

In July 2017, Woods completed a private program to address his dependency on painkillers.

Woods stands alongside his lawyer to face County Judge Darren Steele on Wednesday

In April the Daily Mail broke the news that the golfer would leaving the country 'imminently'

The golf great flipped his Land Rover clean onto its side during his accident in Jupiter

'I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends,' he tweeted at the time. 'I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received.'

Woods' most notorious car crash took place in 2009, when he rammed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant, tree and several hedges near his home.

He was treated for minor injuries and received a ticket for careless driving, but while he thanked his then-wife Elin Nordegren for getting him out of the car, there were lingering doubts about the story. After all, it was only days earlier that the National Enquirer claimed he'd had an affair with Rachel Uchitel, a 9/11 widow and New York nightclub manager.

The alleged details of the November 27, 2009 crash were ultimately included in the best-selling biography by Jeff Benedict and Armen Keteyian, titled Tiger Woods.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe 'kidnap' plot busted: Real Madrid superstar targeted by French gang along with 25 other celebrities - as man is arrested
Sports.content:
Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe was among high-profile figures targeted in a kidnapping plot by a French gang, French authorities have revealed.

The plot reportedly targeted 26 celebrities, including footballers, rappers and wealthy businessmen.

French newspaper Le Parisien reported the plot was allegedly orchestrated by an 18-year-old, named as Clement L.

The gang leader had already been jailed for armed robbery, after being identified as one of two men involved in an attack on a watchmaker in Paris.

It was discovered Clement L had already been on pre-trial detention for pimping, as well as organised robbery.

The gang leader was detained but was then discovered to have been sending orders from his cell via two mobile phones on Snapchat under the alias Lester Z.

Kylian Mbappe was among 26 wealthy individuals targeted in a kidnapping plot in France

A source close to the case told Le Parisien that the addresses of 26 wealthy individuals, including Mbappe, had been discovered on the phones.

The star was among a list including a Chinese businessman, jewellers, and a Turkish meat trader.

'Two phones were seized by prison guards, and their contents were highly revealing,' the source said.

'He also wanted to go after a rapper and the footballer Kylian Mbappe.'

When questioned, the teenager claimed he was not the mastermind of the plot and had requested he be let out of solitary confinement.

He revealed he had dropped out of school while studying for a vocational qualification in cooking but wants to resume studying and become a chef.

Despite his request, it was ruled he remain in solitary confinement while the investigation continues.

Sports.title: Monaco come out fighting amid war of words with Chelsea over collapsed Lamine Camara deal: Transfer chief rejects they are 'the bad guys' - and claims Folarin Balogun walked away from Everton over how they treated him
Sports.content:
Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro has attempted to shed light on their chaotic final day of the transfer window that saw Premier League moves for Folarin Balogun and Lamine Camara collapse.

Balogun had been set to sign for Everton, but issues arose with his medical, at which point Monaco agreed to sell Camara to Chelsea.

However, The Toffees then decided to proceed with the deal after renegotiating terms, meaning the Principality side pulled the plug on Camara's move to Stamford Bridge as they didn't want to lose both players.

Then, at the last moment, Balogun had a change of heart, meaning that he and Camara will stay at the Ligue 1 club, yet Chelsea were left furious by what had gone on.

As a result of the drama, Monaco chief Scuro held a press conference on Wednesday where he launched a staunch defence of his club and insisted that they were not 'the bad guys' in the scenario.

Scuro explained how Monaco were happy to sell Balogun but were desperate to keep Camara, a position that had been communicated to the midfielder earlier on deadline day having rejected several approaches for him over the summer.

Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro has shed light on their chaotic deadline day that saw Premier League moves for both Folarin Balogun and Lamine Camara fall through

Balogun had been set to sign for Everton but he pulled out of the move at the last moment

He said: 'During the day, we had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton. Balogun flew yesterday morning to go for medicals and sign a contract.

'Balogun, besides the salary, was also an important source of income for the club. And then, Lamine would stay.

'This was what we had until mid-afternoon. What happened is that Chelsea were always testing and trying. What about Lamine? What about Lamine? I’ve been talking to them for the last 10 days.

'Around 4PM yesterday, we got a contact from Chelsea. "Okay, we sold a midfielder (Enzo Fernandez). Deal done. Is there any possibility that Monaco are open to selling Lamine?" The answer was the same. No, it’s not. At this moment, at 4PM Balogun was in Liverpool undergoing his medical. Everything was going pretty well.'

Scuro added that at around 7PM, Everton then got in touch about issues with Balogun's medical, 'which for our medical staff, as well as the player's personal medical staff, made no sense at all'.

Although discussions continued with Everton over Balogun's physical health, Scuro explained that Chelsea then went again for Camara and a deal was discussed.

He added: 'And what happened was that around 10PM, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that, OK, there is no problem. We are ready to do it. Let’s sign the contract.

'As soon as we got the information, we came back to Chelsea and thought, "OK, we have our deal there. There is no deal on it (Camara)". Because it’s also fair to do this. It’s also part of the game.

'There is no reason that these kinds of dynamic discussions on the last day of the transfer window, which all of us decided to be on the last day, trying to find solutions, with the clock ticking, that this kind of interaction (sees us) become the bad guys in the room.

'Putting that on Monaco is not fair. So this is the story. We informed, again, everyone that there was no deal with Chelsea. We progressed (with Balogun).'

However, just as the deal was about to be completed, Balogun made the dramatic decision to not proceed with the move having been left upset by Everton's initial concerns surrounding his medical.

Chelsea were left furious after their move for Lamine Camara fell through at the last moment

Scuro said: 'Balogun’s allegation is that "I’m not feeling good because of the way the club treated me. I’m not feeling good because Everton’s medical department raised doubts about my future or my health. I have nothing (no health problem), so I’m not comfortable signing a long contract here."

'And the reality is that when Balo mentioned to us this feeling that he was not comfortable, he didn’t want to sign. We didn’t see ourselves in a position to push him. We had to respect his decision.'

Scuro added that Balogun may still depart in the next few days to a league where the transfer window remains open, while he believes Camara could still move onto 'better things' in the future.

He also insisted he sympathised with both players over their respective sagas.

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: From 'Big Moves Hughes' to Public Enemy No 1 - Saudi-bound transfer chief Richard Hughes has left Reds brutally undercooked, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool Confidential: From 'Big Moves Hughes' to Public Enemy No 1 - Saudi-bound transfer chief Richard Hughes has left Reds brutally undercooked, writes LEWIS STEELE

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Like Arne Slot, history might be kind to Liverpool’s sporting director Richard Hughes – but right now, fans will be in no rush to wave off his farewell plane.

He was the man that recruited Slot himself, after all. When Jurgen Klopp quit, Hughes thought out of the box and identified a replacement that, really, no fan was calling for. Twelve months later, Slot and Hughes were on the Anfield pitch holding aloft the Premier League trophy.

Hughes was also the man who convinced Florian Wirtz to join the club when pretty much every team in Europe fancied him.

A few weeks later, Hughes and Slot handled themselves with class in public statements and private actions when Diogo Jota tragically died in a car crash at just 28.

The Scottish transfer chief was the man who recruited Alexander Isak when the word from Newcastle all summer was that the Swede simply was not for sale.

Neither Isak or Wirtz have flourished just yet but both are showing signs that this could be their year – and that their axis could be frightening for opponents up and down the land.

Richard Hughes was the man who appointed Arne Slot, and together the pair were celebrating the Premier League title a year later. Now the picture looks very different, however

Hughes' big-money purchases of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz are yet to bear fruit

At the end of that record-breaking transfer window in 2025, where Liverpool spent a whopping £446million, Hughes was adored by supporters and made into internet memes. ‘Big Moves Hughes’, one member of the YouTube channel Redmen TV dubbed him.

The poor chap who came up with that nickname is reminded of it every day because a year on, ‘Big Moves Hughes’ is now heading for his own big move – to Saudi Arabia – and few fans will be sad to see him go.

There is a small section of Liverpool fans on social media that seem to spend the majority of their waking hours shouting at screens or sending abusive messages to people they have never met in person.

It says something, then, that Hughes has been public enemy No 1 at times this summer.

This ire comes in a window where they have a bigger net spend than anyone in the league, with one buy just £2million shy of the British transfer record.

Since winning the Premier League title, in fact, Liverpool have spent £693million on first-team players.

So why does everyone dislike Hughes?

The first reason is a stubbornness to strengthen certain positions on the pitch which leave new head coach Andoni Iraola, who Hughes has now recruited at both Bournemouth and Liverpool, brutally undercooked.

Signing Bradley Barcola is a fine bit of business and a potential game-changer – but can the Reds achieve their dreams this season when they are so blatantly light at full back and central midfield?

Signing Bradley Barcola is a fine bit of business and a potential game-changer – but can the Reds achieve their dreams this season when they are so blatantly light in other positions?

Jeremie Frimpong, who has struggled for form this season, is the only fit right back at the club

As they have shown in both games so far, scoring goals will be no issue whatsoever. It is the fact 35-year-old Virgil van Dijk and his new defensive partner Jeremy Jacquet resemble soldiers entering a battlefield with no armour.

You could have the best artillery and weapons in the world but you will not win the war if your troops cannot defend their position, too.

The need for a deeper-lying midfield is not a new thing, nor is it an overreaction to two league fixtures. They have been crying out for one since Fabinho left in 2023, arguably even further when you note the Brazilian started to decline before his exit.

At full back, Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez might come good eventually. For now, though, they are both seismic downgrades on Trent Alexander-Arnold and a prime Andy Robertson.

Frimpong is the only fit right back at the club, with Conor Bradley missing since January with a horrific knee injury. If the Dutchman, noticeably poor in the opening fixtures, gets injured – as he did a lot last term – there is no back-up.

They could ask loanee Ronald Araujo to cover, but he is needed also to cover at centre back where Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni are both on the treatment table. At left back, Kerkez’s deputy is Kostas Tsimikas, who struggled for minutes on loan at Roma last term.

There is a need to be realistic and we know there is no money tree at Anfield. But not signing a midfielder again – and another full back – leaves Liverpool incredibly short. If this turns out to be an unsuccessful season, fan ire may not turn to new boss Iraola but the board.

Given the money spent, it is categorically wrong to accuse anyone of lacking ambition, as some supporters have done. But it is fair to question the plan and ask whether the posh seats give a different view on the game. From where everyone else sits, midfield is a glaring weakness.

As Hughes heads for the exit door, it is hard to escape the feeling that new boss Andoni Iraola has been left short-changed

Instead, most of Hughes’s eggs were in the forward basket. Yankuba Minteh and Ismaila Sarr were targeted but ultimately came to nothing. In fairness, neither made sense: Sarr is 28 and not an upgrade on potential departee Cody Gakpo; Minteh has potential but is injured right now.

Liverpool had known of Mohamed Salah’s exit for half a year yet it felt like they were panicking in the last 10 days of the window.

Leaders Van Dijk and Alisson are both only contracted until the end of this season. Gomez, Tsimikas and Wataru Endo are also in the same boat.

So next summer is already shaping up to be busy as Liverpool feels like a carousel of chaos in a revolving state of transition. It is likely that Hughes will have his feet up in Saudi Arabia, with a move to Al Hilal having been in the works for months.

The sporting director might be remembered more fondly once the likes of Isak and Wirtz click, plus the two wingers he signed this summer – Barcola and Victor Munoz – look like shrewd business.

But as this summer window closes and Hughes heads for the exit door, it is hard to escape the feeling that Iraola has been left short-changed and that, for all the glamorous assets Liverpool have, there are still several design faults not fixed.

Sports.title: Footballer, 20, breaks down in floods of tears alongside his mum after being forced out of his boyhood club due to strict financial rules
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

LaLiga star Pablo Garcia was left in tears after being forced to leave boyhood club Real Betis on deadline day.

Garcia, 20, has been a regular for Betis, playing in all three league games so far this season, but has now put pen to paper on a deal to join Racing Santander.

He joined Betis aged six, and worked his way through the academy ranks to become a first team regular. He played 33 times for the club in total, scoring six goals – including a late winner against Valencia last week.

But, with the club keen to re-sign former Arsenal and Real Madrid man Dani Ceballos, they needed to make quick money and decided to let Garcia go.

He was seen in floods of tears as he left Betis' stadium on Tuesday evening, waving to fans as he wiped his eyes.

Ceballos, 30, was contracted to Madrid for nine years in total, with two of those spent on loan at Arsenal. He had joined Betis as a teenager, playing for them until 2017, when he moved to Madrid.

A teary Pablo Garcia waved goodbye to Real Betis fans on Tuesday as he was sold for financial reasons

Garcia joined Betis at the age of six, but has now left the club for Racing Santander

Due to strict salary limits, Betis was essentially forced to pick between the two players, and chose Ceballos, who signed a three-year deal.

Football fans, though, were left stunned by the decision.

'Shameless!' one fan wrote on X. 'You don't do this to family!'

Another posted: 'Aren't you ashamed?'

A third shared: 'This really is sad. We have to blame [Javier] Tebas [president of LaLiga].'

Garcia told Spanish media: 'It is a very difficult time for everyone, but we have to keep our heads up and look forward. I hope to return, that is what we all want.'

'There were many things I could not influence. I wish everything had gone as we had all hoped. Thank you very much from the bottom of my heart to all Betis fans.'

His father added on RadioCOPE: 'This is really hard for us. If that is how Betis fans feel, imagine how we must feel. It was 15 years, a whole eternity.'

While Ceballos could be in line to make his second debut against former side Madrid this weekend, Betis will take on Rayo Vallecano on Saturday.

The two teams will face off next in December.

Sports.title: Inside Everton's deadline-day shambles: How Folarin Balogun deal collapsed and the early warning signs it was doomed, the Beto gamble that backfired, how David Moyes was let down - and mutinous fans' plans to protest 'unambitious' owners
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish announced his return with the perfect sound bite: 'Every time I see an Everton fan, it's just pure love.'

But come 2pm this Sunday, the darling of Everton's fanbase may have a very different perspective.

When Grealish's white Lamborghini purred out of Everton's Finch Farm training base on Tuesday evening it gave awaiting fans a symbol of hope. Yet, before his engine was but a distant whirr, Everton's deadline day business had not just stalled but gone kaput.

Indeed, a shambolic day's business left manager David Moyes with only one senior striker for the next four months and just 18 outfield players.

It is only a few weeks since chief executive Angus Kinnear branded last season's 13th-place finish as a 'failure' in the eyes of the owners as the Friedkins were 'winners' he said. Then offering the line: 'Everyone is thinking about how we challenge for Europe and don’t fade. Our job in the coming weeks is to ensure the squad has enough depth to mount an even more compelling challenge.'

Yet Moyes can barely fill a squad with senior players against Manchester United on Sunday unless he names two goalkeepers on the bench.

David Moyes has been left short in the transfer market after a deadline day shambles at Everton

The Toffees thought they had a deal for USA star striker Folarin Balogun wrapped up, only for the 25-year-old to walk out of the building

To little surprise, in the wake of Tuesday's business, Everton supporters groups voiced their dissatisfaction with the club's leadership. The Fans' Forum demanded accountability, the Fan Advisory Board asked for answers from Kinnear and the 1878s volunteer group, instrumental in the tifos and banners placed around the stadium on matchdays, declared they were stepping down, because 'we do not feel that our fanbase’s ambitions and the club’s ambitions align right now'.

Further, more vocal, backlash is expected at the Hill Dickinson on Sunday.

Nil Satis Nisi Optimum, nothing but the best is good enough. The club motto that adorns the vast circular ceiling of the first-team dressing room and is branded across the £800million stadium concourse, is regarded now as little more than empty words. A nod to what a proud club once held true.

It was just after midnight when Monaco striker Folarin Balogun declared he no longer wished to sign for Everton.

The player had already been late for his flight over, and Monaco were apparently 'slack' providing the appropriate medical records to help expedite the £40m transfer.

By that stage Everton striker Beto was already being unveiled as a Fiorentina player for a knockdown £15m.

Had Balogun got on his scheduled flight in the morning, and Monaco been more forthcoming, Everton argue they would have had greater time to identify and rectify the situation so much sooner.

As it transpired, 'a significant issue' was identified with the USA international's medical. The 25-year-old, who had played in the World Cup with heavy strapping on his left knee, sat and waited as a solution was sought.

EVERTON'S DEADLINE DAY FROM HELL - AS IT HAPPENED 9am: Everton begin the day intent on signing Jack Grealish, Folarin Balogun and Kenny Tete, with a few more targets on their radar. 11am: As the day goes on, it becomes apparent the deal for Tete is off, with Fulham's bid for Rayo Vallecano's Andrei Ratu falling through. 12pm: Everton agree a deal for alternative right-back option Ainsley Maitland-Niles, whom they tried to sign in 2021. He jets in from France, as does Balogun. 3pm: Balogun begins his medical in the afternoon, later than expected, and issues are raised by Everton's medical staff, throwing the deal in doubt. The Toffees try to renegotiate a lower fee with his club, Monaco. 6pm: Everton sanction the sale of back-up striker Beto, leaving Thierno Barry as the only centre forward at the club. 8pm: Full back Nathan Patterson is sold to Torino for just £1million, leaving Everton with no cover at both right back and left back. 9pm: Star man Iliman Ndiaye heads to Man City for a bargain £65million. 9.10pm: With the Balogun deal in jeopardy, Everton make a last-ditch move for Man United's Joshua Zirkzee on loan, having been rejected by Aston Villa's Tammy Abraham. It proves unsuccessful. 10pm: Midfielder Tim Iroegbunam, liked by boss David Moyes, joins Hull in a £22million deal. 10.10pm: The loan signing of Grealish is confirmed. 10.20pm: Everton and Monaco reach an agreement over a reduced fee for Balogun and it appears the Toffees will get their man after all. 10.55pm: Everton submit a deal sheet to the Premier League to get the Balogun deal over the line. Midnight: Everton confirm the addition of Maitland-Niles. 12:15am: The Balogun deal falls through when the player has a change of heart in light of Everton's doubts over his fitness and pursuit of other strikers. Everton are left with one centre forward, one left back and one right back at the club - and with their fans in mutiny.

Calls went out to Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and to Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham. A £10m loan deal was offered to United but rejected at 9.30pm. Abraham wanted to stay.

Word was out the deal was in jeopardy.

Everton officials restructured the fee with Monaco to a much lower figure with an appearance-related trigger for additional payments. Monaco agreed so both clubs and the player signed the deal sheet just before 11pm. The press were notified.

An hour later, and with the final stages of the deal being tidied up, Balogun, aware Everton had searched for alternative solutions, made it clear he wanted to go back to Monaco.

How could this happen?

Balogun had become Moyes's priority even before it became evident last Sunday that the club were attempting to complete a £35m deal to re-sign Richarlison with Iliman Ndiaye, the club's best player, going the other way to Tottenham for £60m.

That idea had been dismissed then accelerated in the direction Ndiaye wanted when Manchester City stepped in to sign him after seeing Cody Gakpo could not be prised from Liverpool.

Still, £65m was at least £15m under market price for a 26-year-old with three years left on contract.

The loan return of Jack Grealish was one of the few things Evertonians could celebrate on deadline day

Everton's talisman Iliman Ndiaye headed for Man City in a deal below his market value

Ndiaye had wanted to leave Everton for much of the summer and told officials that was the case. He’d rejected several contract offers, so his sale was expected. As was Beto's but Italy's earlier transfer deadline of 7pm meant Everton always ran the risk of him departing without having a replacement, and so it transpired.

Perhaps the warning signs about the club's true financial status were already there.

Days previously, a £2m deal for Manchester United's 20-year-old striker Ethan Wheatley had been put in place. All was agreed, only for Everton to pull back. Financial priorities lay elsewhere.

Then came the incendiary news that the club had agreed to sell Harrison Armstrong, an academy graduate, one of their own, to Nottingham Forest for £40m.

At Bournemouth that day, travelling supporters made their feelings clear: 'Don't sell Armstrong, you're going to have a riot on your hands.' Their chant aimed at the watching Kinnear and who he represents.

'We still need to add players to what we've got,' Moyes warned later. 'I've been saying it for quite a while.

'If I have a message to the supporters? Their manager is an Evertonian.'

Dan Friedkin himself was apparently instrumental in ensuring Armstrong stayed and Moyes must have thought the proverbial fire had been put out. That he could look forward.

However, by Monday evening it was known that Ndiaye would head for City, and that Tim Iroegbunam – a midfielder liked by Moyes – would seal a £22m switch to Hull. With Beto’s sale to Italy included, Everton had recouped almost £100m.

Nathan Patterson was allowed to join Torino for £1m on the proviso another right back was coming in. That was Fulham's Kenny Tete, whom Everton had tried to sign on a free 12 months ago, but that ran into issues.

Serious doubts now exist among Everton fans about the wisdom and commitment of owners the Friedkin Group (Dan Friedkin pictured with his son Ryan)

Strengthening that position, something even Prime Minister Andy Burnham had pleaded for, was crucial. Moyes’s prime target was Strasbourg’s Guela Doue but the recruitment team wouldn’t make the necessary £30m investment. With the route to Tete blocked they went back to France for Lyon's £3m utility player Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

When Chelsea came calling with the offer of £65m for James Garner on Tuesday evening, Moyes must have wondered what challenge could possibly come next.

Jamie Vardy or Anthony Martial on a free perhaps? Not yet, at least.

An avid reader, the Scot once professed to turning to the musings of the great explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton for inspiration in ways to lead his teams. Shackleton's famous ship was called Endurance, and Moyes will need all he can muster to see this expedition through with the Friedkins at the helm.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
