Sports.title: Austin Williams Tests Vito Mielnicki’s Contender Claims
Sports.content:
Gardzielik was dropped and lost every round on all three scorecards. Nmomah offered limited resistance before being stopped in the ninth. Huerta went the distance but lost 100-90, 100-90, and 99-91. Those victories showed Mielnicki can dominate carefully selected opposition. They did not demonstrate that he is prepared for a championship fight.

Top Rank moved Mielnicki methodically by matching him against fighters with attractive records but little recognition in the United States. The approach helped him collect regional belts and climb the sanctioning-body rankings without facing anyone near the top of the middleweight class.

The more revealing performances came against Khalil El Harraz and Connor Coyle. Mielnicki edged El Harraz by majority decision and then struggled to a majority draw with Coyle. The New York State Athletic Commission later changed the Coyle result to a no-contest after he tested positive for performance-enhancing drugs, but the ruling did not erase what happened during those 10 rounds.

Mielnicki believes beating Williams would answer criticism of rankings that place him No. 3 with the WBO, No. 7 with the WBA and WBC, and No. 9 with the IBF.

“I feel like having a name like him on my resume will silence a lotta that,” Mielnicki told Keith Idec of The Ring.

Williams (20-2, 13 KOs) is a considerable upgrade. The physically strong southpaw applies pressure and can make Mielnicki fight while moving backward, an area that the trio was not equipped to test. Mielnicki must show that his footwork and inside game hold up when an opponent closes the distance and refuses to remain at his preferred pace.

Still, beating Williams would not establish Mielnicki as one of the best at 160. Hamzah Sheeraz stopped Williams, and Carlos Adames defeated him decisively over 12 rounds. Williams occupies the middle of the first tier: capable enough to expose a protected contender, but well below the elite.

That makes him an appropriate screening test. A Mielnicki loss in his New Jersey backyard would make his lofty rankings difficult to defend. A convincing win would earn him the opportunity to face the leading middleweights, not prove he is ready to beat them.

Sports.title: Hearn Disputes Kremlev’s Bivol-Beterbiev Trilogy Offer Claim
Sports.content:
“It was never offered, by the way,” said Hearn during a media scrum reported by ProBox TV . “If there was an offer that was even remotely reasonable, the Callum Smith fight wouldn’t be happening. Dmitry would have vacated and fought Beterbiev.”

That version is difficult to reconcile with Kremlev’s account. The IBA president said negotiations had taken place with both camps and that Bivol was offered twice his previous purse. Kremlev also claimed Beterbiev was willing to box without taking a purse to help complete the trilogy.

The dispute may come down to the difference between vocal backing and an actionable contract. A public promise of enormous money is not the same as written terms containing a date, venue, broadcaster, payment schedule, guarantees, and regulatory responsibilities.

Beterbiev’s reported willingness to compete for free demonstrates his desire for the fight, but it does not provide a workable economic structure. His purse was only one part of the proposed event. Someone still had to guarantee Bivol’s money and cover the considerable production and promotional costs.

Mandatory obligations have also dismantled the undisputed championship created by their first two fights. Bivol relinquished the WBC belt rather than defend against David Benavidez, then satisfied his IBF requirement. Facing Smith under the WBO order would place another challenger between Bivol and the trilogy.

Smith provides a useful common opponent. Beterbiev stopped him in seven rounds in January 2024, overpowering the former super middleweight champion with sustained pressure. A clear Bivol victory would invite comparisons, although their contrasting styles make a direct measurement unreliable. Beterbiev broke Smith physically; Bivol would be more likely to dismantle him through distance, timing, and combinations.

Delay carries a heavier price for Beterbiev. He has not fought since losing the rematch in February 2025, while Bivol returned against Michael Eifert and is preparing for Smith. At 41, Beterbiev cannot recover lost time through another training camp.

If the trilogy is postponed until 2027, Beterbiev may have spent nearly two years outside the ring. The eventual fight would still sell, but it might no longer settle the rivalry under conditions resembling their first two meetings. What began as a 50-50 conclusion risks becoming a test of how much age and inactivity have taken from Beterbiev.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Admits Early Success Cost Him Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
“I felt a bit too comfortable maybe with the really early knockdown, then followed by another one in the third,” Wardley said during the kick-off press conference. “I thought this is near on a foregone conclusion. I’ve done it once, I’ve done it twice, I can get him out of there. “I was a victim of my own success in them early stages. I just got trigger-happy, got carried away with trying to launch that right hand. In the moments when I did have him hurt, I don’t actually think I jumped on him enough.”

The mistake was not simply failing to throw enough punches. Wardley stopped disguising the right hand and began loading up from too far away. Dubois steadied himself behind a stiff jab, controlled the distance, and forced him to expend more energy each time he attempted to close the space.

The challenger needs greater variety in London. Hooks to the ribs would give Dubois something else to consider behind his tight guard, while doubling the lead hook may create a cleaner route for Wardley’s power. Hunting for one spectacular shot only makes his attack easier to read.

Pacing will be just as important. An early knockdown does not require an immediate all-out assault, particularly in a fight scheduled for 12 rounds. Wardley must allow his successes to count on the scorecards without emptying his energy reserves in search of a dramatic finish.

The five-month turnaround adds another concern. Wardley absorbed sustained punishment before the 11th-round stoppage and has gone directly into another demanding camp without an interim bout. He dismissed questions about his condition, saying he had “absolutely zero excuses” for the defeat or the rematch.

Dubois carries the psychological advantage. He knows he can withstand Wardley’s heaviest punches, regain command with his jab, and break him down over the later rounds. The harder mental test for Wardley may arrive if he lands cleanly again and the champion refuses to fold.

The first fight established that Wardley can hurt Dubois. On October 17, he must show that early success will sharpen his decisions instead of distorting them.

Sports.title: Janibek Corners Hamzah Sheeraz Before WBO Deadline
Sports.content:
Sheeraz has already built a possible defense for refusing the fight. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, he called the WBO’s ruling a “joke” and criticized the organization for rewarding Janibek after his positive test for meldonium.

The clean-sport objection has merit. The WBO shortened Janibek’s suspension, allowed him to move directly into a mandatory position at 168 pounds, and selected him over Jacob Bank despite Janibek never fighting in the division. Bank had actively campaigned at super middleweight and petitioned for the same opportunity.

Still, Sheeraz’s moral position also provides a convenient exit. He can vacate while claiming he refused to cooperate with a sanctioning body order he considers disgraceful, rather than admitting that Janibek presents too much danger for too little money.

Surrendering the title would harm Sheeraz’s reputation. He won the vacant belt against 39-year-old Alem Begic and struggled through a majority verdict over Simon Zachenhuber in his first defense. Leaving before facing Janibek would support the Kazakh’s claim that Sheeraz was only a “champion by name.”

Facing Janibek carries the greater career risk. He is a precise southpaw counterpuncher with the power to punish the defensive lapses Sheeraz showed against Zachenhuber. A decisive loss would cost Sheeraz his belt and reduce his value for larger fights against Canelo Alvarez or Chris Eubank Jr.

The history makes an escape harder to disguise. Sheeraz withdrew from negotiations when the WBO ordered him to challenge Janibek at middleweight. After Sheeraz moved to 168 and became champion, Janibek followed him into the division.

Vacating can be presented as a principled business choice. Getting stopped by the opponent who pursued him through two weight classes would be far worse. Janibek has left Sheeraz to choose which consequence he is willing to accept.

Sports.title: Two Minutes in Tokyo: George Foreman Slaughters José Roman
Sports.content:
Roman had little chance of testing him. The Puerto Rican challenger stood 5-foot-10 and weighed between 196½ and 197 pounds, leaving him considerably smaller than the 6-foot-4, 219-pound champion. He had been outside the rankings when the fight was signed before being elevated to No. 9 by the WBA and WBC.

That placement gave the promotion official legitimacy, but it did not make Roman a genuine threat. Foreman was 38-0 with 35 knockouts and had just destroyed Frazier in two rounds to seize the championship. Roman brought a 43-7-1 or 44-7-1 record, depending on the source, with 21 knockouts.

Once the bell rang, even two minutes proved too long.

Foreman did not merely follow Roman and swing wildly. Under trainer Dick Sadler, he had learned to take broad lateral steps that closed escape routes. His lead hand served as more than a jab. He posted it against Roman, pushed him off balance, and turned him toward the right hand.

That rough leverage helped Foreman control opponents before the power punches landed. Some of it crossed into boxing’s gray area, particularly when he shoved or extended his lead arm, but Roman lacked the strength and composure to resist it.

The destruction of Frazier also followed Foreman into the ring. Roman knew that six knockdowns had reduced the previous champion to a helpless target. His tense movement and reluctance to commit gave Foreman little reason to respect anything coming back.

Foreman cut down the available space, drove Roman toward the ropes, and attacked his body. Roman fell along the ropes near the one-minute point, but referee Jay Edson initially treated it as a slip or loss of balance rather than a knockdown.

The decision became controversial when Foreman landed a right while Roman was sitting on the canvas. Roman’s manager, Bill Daly, and trainer, Al Braverman, jumped onto the apron demanding a disqualification. Edson ruled that Foreman had been following through and that the punch carried little force. Because the original fall was ruled a slip, Roman received neither a mandatory count nor additional recovery time.

The challenger rose, only to be dropped by a right hand. Roman made it up once more, but Foreman finished him with a right uppercut at exactly 2:00 of the opening round. Roman’s corner later called Foreman “the dirtiest fighter in the world,” while some members of the Tokyo crowd booed the abrupt ending.

Roman’s ranking exposed the business behind the defense. He was outside the WBA and WBC ratings when the fight was arranged, then elevated to No. 9 so the organizations could approve him as a challenger. The placement did not make him a mandatory contender or establish championship credentials. It allowed an overseas title defense to proceed against an opponent selected for limited risk.

Promoters advertised Foreman’s purse as $1 million, a figure that became attached to the fight in later records. Contemporary reporting placed his actual guarantee near $250,000, while other accounts and Foreman’s later recollections put his earnings in the $250,000 to $300,000 range. Roman received approximately $100,000.

Attendance reached roughly 7,500 to 8,000 in an arena capable of holding nearly twice that number. The midday Saturday scheduling and expensive tickets hurt local sales, leaving Japanese promoters braced for a financial loss despite televising the bout free to domestic viewers.

Foreman followed the Roman destruction by stopping Ken Norton in two rounds the next year. Across the Frazier, Roman, and Norton fights, he needed only five rounds to dispose of three heavyweights who had a combined 91 professional victories.

The two-minute result also concealed a flaw that Muhammad Ali later exploited. Foreman committed heavily to his power punches and expected resistance to collapse under the first sustained attack. Roman rewarded that approach by folding almost immediately.

Ali refused to provide the same response in Zaire the following year. He forced Foreman to keep punching after the quick finish failed to materialize, turning the champion’s aggression and confidence in his strength into an exhausting trap.

Foreman’s comeback decades later produced one of boxing’s greatest stories, capped by the heavyweight championship at age 45. Yet the older Foreman relied more on patience, positioning, and conservation. The 1973 version brought something more frightening: youth, crushing strength, and an appetite for immediate destruction.

Roman was never equipped to disprove it.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says Crawford Resents His Boxing Takeover
Sports.content:
“I gave my honest opinion, saying that he left a lot on the table. That’s all I said. Crawford is the one that’s always coming up and slightly hating on me little by little. In the meantime, you’re retired. You should be in Turks and Caicos chilling on a yacht, enjoying your family. He’s desperate, bro,” said Ryan to Fight Hub TV. “Nobody knows him outside of boxing, so he’s doing everything he can to continue his name. He actually likes the attention. I used to think Crawford didn’t, but now I know he does. He realized nobody cares after you retire.”

Ryan also dismissed Crawford’s presence at Benn’s gym. “I feel like I’ll beat your ass, so what are you going to teach him?” he said.

Their bad blood highlights the fundamental difference between the two men. Crawford pursued championships, pound-for-pound recognition, and technical supremacy. Garcia measures his position through audience size, financial leverage, and the ability to command boxing’s most valuable dates.

Crawford built the greater traditional legacy, but Ryan attracts the larger mainstream audience. If Garcia defeats Benn and becomes boxing’s leading commercial figure, he will have achieved something Crawford never managed despite accomplishing far more inside the ring.

Working with Benn does not necessarily prove Garcia’s accusation that Crawford craves attention. It may represent a retired fighter transferring his knowledge to another contender. Garcia has turned that mentorship into an insult, reducing Benn to a pupil who cannot be saved even by one of boxing’s finest technicians.

That approach also keeps Benn’s abilities outside the discussion. By treating the fight as a proxy battle with Crawford, Garcia portrays him as little more than the vehicle for another man’s resentment.

The claim brings considerable risk. Garcia’s argument carries force only if he beats Benn. A loss would damage his attempt to place drawing power above championships while giving Crawford every reason to question both his boxing and his self-appointed status.

The message was simple: Crawford had his run and should either return to face someone such as Jaron Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr. or stay quiet in retirement.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Faces Duty as Oleksandr Usyk Exits
Sports.content:
The champion would naturally prefer a larger fight. Revenge against Dubois carries commercial value after Hrgovic’s stoppage loss to him in 2024, while a unification would pay considerably more than defending against Sanchez. The IBF mandate leaves little room for shopping around unless Sanchez accepts another step-aside agreement.

Dubois first has his own business to settle. He defends the WBO title against Fabio Wardley in their October 17 rematch at London’s O2 Arena. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May meeting, but the punishment he absorbed makes the return dangerous. Hrgovic cannot build his plans around Dubois retaining.

Oleksandr Usyk is operating outside that championship traffic. The former unified champion is targeting Deontay Wilder for a final fight in the United States in 2027. It offers Usyk one more famous name, but little clarity about the division’s best heavyweight.

Usyk struggled more than anticipated against boxing novice Rico Verhoeven in May. He trailed on one scorecard and was level on the other two before producing an 11th-round stoppage. Wilder also carries the wear of a long career and no longer releases his right hand with the conviction that once made him boxing’s most feared puncher. Their proposed fight sells history and name recognition rather than determining the division’s leader.

The active championship race now belongs to Hrgovic, Dubois, WBA champion Murat Gassiev, and WBC interim champion Agit Kabayel. Gassiev stopped Peter Kadiru in six rounds in July, while Kabayel demolished Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. A Gassiev-Kabayel unification would immediately reduce the number of competing titleholders.

Hrgovic wants access to those lucrative fights, but Sanchez remains positioned directly in front of him. Beating Itauma won Hrgovic the belt. Defeating his mandatory would prove that he can keep it.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Waits for the Winner of Canelo-Mbilli
Sports.content:
Martinez was much more effective and landed the harder punches. Lester had the support of the Guatemalan people with a healthy attendance of 6,848 at the USC Galen Center. The interim WBC super middleweight champion is the only boxing champion of any kind for Guatemala; Martinez is held in high esteem, receiving the full support of his country. After the victory, he celebrated at Lafayette Park at the Festival Chapin with his fellow countrymen.

ProBox promoter Garry Jonas stated at the post-fight press conference they’re exploring the options of holding a Lester Martinez fight at a soccer stadium somewhere in Guatemala, hopefully for January of 2027. The energy and crowd at the Galen Center was electrifying as the crowd would erupt in cheers every time Lester would land a big punch.

Holding an event in Guatemala would definitely draw a crowd. Lester is becoming a bigger star with every fight, and if he’s able to secure a fight with the winner of the Canelo Alvarez-Christian Mbilli fight, he would only become that much bigger. Trainer Esau Dieguez said of the fight, “The truth is we would like to face the winner, but because of name recognition and what it would bring, we would like to fight Canelo. Being that we already fought Mbilli, but I expect Canelo to win. I think Canelo will win, I hope we can make the fight. I know the WBC may beat around the bush, but our hope is Lester will fight for the full world title.”

It was the fight against Mbilli that raised Lester’s profile and introduced him to the world. Although it was ruled a draw, there are many who believe Martinez should have been awarded the decision. Lester stood toe-to-toe with the power puncher, exchanging punch for punch with him. Martinez outlanded Mbilli 412 to 273 in total punches, outlanding him in 9 of 12 rounds (Compubox).

He tried securing the rematch with Christian, but the fight never materialized. Expecting a tough fight against the Canelo-Mbilli winner, Lester said, “I think for now I will relax, but I know what is coming will be more difficult, and we will prepare for it.”

Knowing that he will have to perform at his absolute best against whomever the winner may be. Lester has proven he has the skills to compete at the championship level, and he has the full support of an entire country with him in Guatemala; they want nothing more than to have their first full world champion.

Ghana News.title: Ghana leather manufacturers demand lower tariffs, threaten demonstration over high costs
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Leather and Footwear Manufacturers Association has threatened to hit the streets if the government fails to reduce import duties on raw materials used by local manufacturers.

The Association says high tariffs are driving up the cost of producing footwear locally, leaving Ghanaian manufacturers at a disadvantage against imported products.

It has consequently petitioned Parliament, calling for an urgent review of the current tariff regime and stronger enforcement at the ports.

Speaking to the media after submitting the petition to the Clerk of Parliament, President of the Association, Gilbert Ntim, said the high cost of production is crippling the local leather and footwear industry, with some factories being forced to shut down.

He outlined two key demands from the government.

“Our demand to government is lower tariffs. Two, strict enforcement at the Tema Port on finished synthetic leather goods coming from China.”

Mr Ntim said the current situation risks undermining efforts to develop a sustainable local manufacturing industry.

“When the local producers don’t have room to operate, this becomes economic sabotage. Why do we sponsor our enemies to kill us? It’s like the system is not working for Ghanaian producers; it is rather favouring foreigners more than us.”

He warned that the Association would resort to street action if its concerns are not addressed.

“So, if our demands are not met, the government will hear our voices on the streets,” he said.

According to Mr Ntim, the impact extends beyond manufacturers, with artisans and young people who depend on the leather and footwear industry for employment also at risk.

He said the continued closure of factories was contributing to job losses and weakening efforts to establish a viable domestic leather and footwear manufacturing sector.

“A nation that cannot foot its people walks into the future with bare feet.”

Mr Ntim further called for stricter enforcement of existing laws to protect local manufacturers from unfair competition.

“The law must be applied vigorously to protect local producers. We are not here just to speak,” he added.

The Association is therefore urging government to urgently review import duties on raw materials and strengthen checks at the Tema Port, particularly on finished synthetic leather products.

It says the measures are necessary to reduce production costs, protect local manufacturers, safeguard jobs and ensure the survival and growth of Ghana’s leather and footwear industry.

Ghana News.title: Roads Minister threatens to terminate Techiman–Nkonsia–Wenchi road contract
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Roads and Highways, Governs Kwame Agbodza, has warned that government will terminate the contract of Volta Impex Construction if the company does not speed up work on the 32-kilometre Techiman–Nkonsia–Wenchi road.

Agbodza said the contractor has ignored repeated warnings from the Ghana Highway Authority to meet its progress targets. The project should have reached 15 to 20 per cent completion by now but stands at just six per cent.

During a site inspection as part of a tour of selected road projects in the Bono, Bono East, Upper West, Upper East, and Northern Regions, the minister warned that government would not tolerate the delays any longer.

He said a decision on the future of the contract would be taken after a meeting with the contractor scheduled for Monday, September 7.

“The contractor hasn’t shown enough commitment to complete this job. Some mobilisation has been paid, and the contractor is not here. We’ll make a firm decision on Monday, [September 7],” he said.

According to the minister, the slow pace of work is unacceptable, especially after the contractor received GH¢66 million in mobilisation payment in May to commence and accelerate work on the project.

Ghana News.title: Beyond compliance: Industrial resilience as a strategic component of national security
Ghana News.content:
From Ukraine’s battlefields to NATO’s latest initiatives, recent developments show that maintaining military advantage depends on more than acquiring advanced technology. It requires the ability to move promising ideas from research to the front line quickly, efficiently, and at scale.

Military advantage is no longer defined by numbers alone. Increasingly, it depends on how quickly armed forces can identify emerging technologies and translate them into battlefield capability.

In an era of strategic competition, innovation has become as fundamental to national defence as training, logistics and operational planning.

The war in Ukraine has underscored this shift. Commercial drones, satellite communications and artificial intelligence-enabled software have been integrated into military operations far more quickly than traditional procurement cycles would have allowed.

These capabilities have enhanced reconnaissance, battlefield awareness and precision targeting, while exposing the limitations of acquisition systems that often take years to deliver new equipment.

The conflict has shown that the ability to adopt and employ new technology quickly can shape military outcomes as decisively as conventional firepower.

Beyond compliance, today’s defence environment demands more than merely meeting procurement procedures or technical certification. Armed forces must identify promising technologies early, assess them rigorously and field them before operational requirements change.

In response, many governments are expanding collaboration with technology companies, universities and research institutions, creating faster pathways from research and development to military application.

NATO has made this approach a strategic priority through the Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) and the NATO Innovation Fund.

Together, these initiatives support research into artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, autonomous systems, biotechnology and resilient communications, and connect innovators with defence organisations across the Alliance. Their objective is to accelerate the adoption of emerging technologies and to strengthen Allied readiness for future challenges.

The industry is evolving alongside these efforts. Digital engineering, advanced manufacturing and advanced simulation are shortening development timelines and improving the design, testing and production of defence systems.

At the same time, lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic and recent conflicts have reinforced the importance of resilient supply chains for critical military equipment. Industrial resilience is now recognised as a strategic component of national security.

Technology alone, however, cannot guarantee military effectiveness. Skilled personnel, experienced leadership and realistic training remain essential to the successful integration of new capabilities. Continued investment in people ensures that technological advances can be applied confidently, responsibly and effectively in demanding operational conditions.

Defence innovation is ultimately about maintaining military readiness in an unpredictable world. Nations that shorten the path from research to deployment, strengthen cooperation across government, industry and academia, and invest in a highly skilled workforce will be better placed to deter aggression, support allies and respond to emerging threats.

In modern defence, the decisive advantage will belong not simply to those who develop the most advanced technologies, but to those who can transform them into battlefield capability more quickly than their competitors.

Ghana News.title: What if “I’m fine” isn’t fine?
Ghana News.content:
There is a version of mental illness that many of us recognise. It is the person who can no longer get out of bed, has stopped going to work or attending lectures, withdrawn from everyone and is visibly struggling. Someone who has, for all intents and purposes, stopped living.

But there is another version we do not recognise as easily: the person who is still functioning while quietly falling apart.

They go to work. They answer messages. They attend family events. They laugh. They meet deadlines. They live their lives. They may even be the person everyone calls when something goes wrong.

And yet, inside, they may be exhausted, overwhelmed, burnt out and hurting in ways nobody sees.

The myth of the “legitimate” breakdown

One of the most damaging ideas around mental health is that a person must reach a crisis or breaking point before their pain becomes legitimate enough to warrant help or intervention.

Somewhere along the way, we convinced ourselves that “I am still managing” is proof that everything is fine.

We have been made to believe that the fact that we are able to complete tasks, show up to work, attend classes and stick to our schedules, sometimes even to our own detriment, means we are okay. It is not.

The World Health Organization defines mental health as a state of well-being that enables people to cope with the stresses of life, realise their abilities, learn and work well, and contribute to their communities. Mental health is classified as a basic human right and is tied to how people think, feel, relate to others, and function daily.

It is not simply the absence of a mental disorder.

That distinction is important.

A person can continue functioning in some areas of life while experiencing significant emotional or psychological distress. Mental health exists on a continuum, and people's experiences are shaped by individual, family, community and broader social and structural factors.

In other words, mental-health struggles do not always announce themselves dramatically.

Sometimes they look like exhaustion, irritability, withdrawing from people while still showing up to work. Sometimes they look like someone who is laughing loudly in public and crying quietly at home. And sometimes they look like someone who has become exceptionally good at pretending everything is fine.

Ghana's treatment gap

This tension is especially stark in Ghana, where stigma, cultural beliefs and limited mental-health literacy have historically contributed to delayed help-seeking.

According to a 2026 World Health Organization publication on expanding mental-health coverage under Ghana's National Health Insurance Scheme, these barriers have historically restricted access to care, while treatment coverage for several mental-health conditions remains extremely low.

Drawing on a 2021 WHO Special Initiative for Mental Health situational assessment, the publication reported estimated national treatment rates ranging from just 0.61% for major depressive disorder to 33.21% for schizophrenia.

In other words, a significant proportion of people living with mental-health conditions are not receiving care.

The barriers are not only about stigma.

Ghana has also faced shortages in mental-health professionals and an uneven distribution of services.

Specialist mental-health care has historically been concentrated in a small number of psychiatric facilities, creating additional geographical and financial barriers for people who live far from them.

A 2026 WHO assessment also noted that Ghana's mental-health system has historically been under-resourced, although the country is taking steps to expand access and integrate mental-health services into primary healthcare.

These realities should force us to rethink what we actually mean when we tell people to “seek help.”

Because telling someone to seek help is only meaningful if help is accessible, affordable and socially acceptable.

Help should not be reserved for emergencies

We should be able to view therapy and mental-health care as part of preventative healthcare, the same way we view routine checkups.

If it is not unusual to visit a hospital because we have a persistent headache, stomach pain, body pains or some other physical discomfort, we should be equally comfortable speaking to a mental-health professional when we notice that our mood has changed, our relationships are suffering, our sleep has deteriorated or we have been carrying an emotional weight we cannot quite identify or put down. We should not have to wait until all of that tips into crisis.

There is another reason this matters: people who appear to be high-functioning are often rewarded for hiding their distress.

The more capable or put-together someone appears, the less likely those around them may be to ask how they are really doing.

We assume that because they are meeting deadlines, taking care of their families, going to work and making everyone laugh, they must be fine.

Sometimes the person everyone describes as “strong” is simply someone who has become very good at functioning while hurting.

Changing the approach

Our overall approach to mental health needs to change.

We need to stop treating it as a foreign, frightening or overly complicated concept and start viewing it for what it is: an essential part of our overall wellbeing.

The first step is demystifying mental health and challenging the stigma attached to people who are brave enough to talk about their struggles and seek help.

We need to stop romanticizing pain simply because it is endured quietly.

We also need to stop dismissing people who express their emotions freely as “overly emotional”, “dramatic” or “too sensitive”.

Emotions are part of being human. Expressing them does not make us weak.

We need to understand that just as different parts of our physical bodies can experience problems that require medical attention, our mental health can also experience challenges that require professional intervention.

Needing a psychologist, psychiatrist, counsellor or other qualified professional does not make someone “mad”. Taking psychiatric medication does not make someone less of a person. Asking for help does not mean someone has failed.

It means they recognized that something was wrong and decided to do something about it.

We also need to move away from the idea that mental-health struggles are necessarily spiritual problems or moral failures.

Faith can be an important source of support. So can family, friendship and community. But none of these should prevent someone from accessing professional care when they need it.

Mental health deserves the same seriousness we give to our physical health. And perhaps one of the simplest changes we can make is to stop waiting for people to collapse before we believe them.

Ask your friend who always says they are fine. Check on the person who is always checking on everyone else.

Pay attention to the person who has suddenly become unusually withdrawn.

And if someone tells you they are struggling, resist the urge to immediately tell them to “be strong”. Sometimes they do not need another reminder to be strong.

They need to know that they do not have to carry everything alone.

We can start seeking help when we notice that something has changed, rather than waiting until we can no longer function. We can learn to recognize distress before it becomes a crisis.

And we can create a culture where asking for help is not treated as an admission of weakness, but recognized for what it actually is: an investment in staying well.

You do not have to be falling apart to deserve support. Sometimes asking for help early is precisely what prevents you from falling apart later.

Ghana News.title: Nigerian music lawyer Akinyemi Ayinoluwa reveals factors driving Nigeria’s music success
Ghana News.content:
Nigerian music lawyer and founder of Amelia Songs, Akinyemi Ayinoluwa, has identified some factors that contribute to the impressive performance of the Nigerian music industry.

Speaking in an interview on Cruise Control with Merqury Quaye and Maame Adwoa Akotaah on Hitz 103.9 FM, Ayinoluwa said Nigeria’s large population provides its creative talents with a sizeable domestic market and a strong numerical advantage.

“One of the things we have going on for the Nigerian talents is the power of numbers and the population. It kind of gives them an advantage,” he said.

Ayinoluwa further described Nigerians as “flamboyant,” “loud mouthed” and “braggadocious”, arguing that these characteristics can sometimes translate into confidence and aggression in the pursuit of success within the entertainment industry.

According to Ayinoluwa, Nigerians are also naturally competitive, and the willingness to compete and constantly seek to outdo one another has become a driving force for some Nigerian creatives.

“So I think the edge would be like the attitude and the aggression to outdo,” he explained. “You know, with Nigerians, immediately you do a two-million-dollar deal, the other Nigerian wants to do a three-million-dollar deal. Nigerians are very competitive,” he indicated.

Beyond the domestic market, Ayinoluwa believes the size of the Nigerian diaspora also contributes to the international reach of Nigerian music.

“And also I think the diasporan population all over the world also helps,” he added.

Who is Akinyemi Ayinoluwa?

Ayinoluwa is an entertainment lawyer and founder and managing partner of Hightower Solicitors and Advocates, where he specialises in music law and represents recording artists, songwriters, record producers, record labels, music investors and talent managers.

He has spent more than a decade advocating for the rights of songwriters and record producers, whom he has previously described as some of the most underrepresented players in the music industry.

In 2025, Ayinoluwa was named among Billboard’s Top Music Lawyers, becoming the only Nigerian lawyer featured on the list that year. Billboard highlighted his work representing major Afrobeats producers and his involvement in music publishing and rights negotiations.

His firm has represented producers including Magicsticks, Ragee, Rexxie, Blaq Jerzee, Masterkraft and Marvey Musique, among others.

Ayinoluwa also has experience as a musician, having previously worked as a songwriter, recording artist and performer before establishing himself in entertainment law.

His comments come amid continued conversations about the differing trajectories of the Ghanaian and Nigerian music industries, particularly Nigeria’s growing global footprint in Afrobeats and the need for Ghanaian talents to expand their reach beyond the local market.

Ghana News.title: Boards’ dissolution: Mahama won’t tolerate indiscipline, poor performance – Secretary
Ghana News.content:
FILE PHOTO: Ghana's President-elect John Dramani Mahama, 66, speaks with Reuters journalists in his office after general elections, in Accra, Ghana, December 13, 2024. REUTERS/Francis Kokoroko/File Photo - RC2GOBADLRFY

President John Dramani Mahama has issued a strong warning to ministers, chief executives, board members and other political appointees that conduct undermining government cohesion, institutional authority and the implementation of government policy will not be tolerated.

The warning comes on the heels of the President’s dissolution of the boards of nine state institutions and follows recent ministerial changes, with an impending reshuffle of chief executives also expected.

In a notice issued by the Secretary to the President, Dr Callistus Mahama, all political appointees were reminded of the President’s resolve to enforce discipline, accountability and effective leadership across government.

“The President expects all Ministers, Deputy Ministers, Chief Executives, Board members and other political appointees to discharge their responsibilities with integrity, diligence, humility and respect for established administrative procedures,” the notice stated.

It cautioned that “conduct that undermines governmental cohesion, institutional authority or the effective implementation of Government policy will not be tolerated.”

The notice also signals that the administration’s scrutiny of its appointees will extend beyond the latest changes, with performance assessments continuing across government.

“Performance across all sectors will continue to be assessed, and the President will take any further action necessary to safeguard the integrity, effectiveness and responsiveness of his Administration,” it stated.

The latest warning follows President Mahama’s decision on Wednesday, September 2, to dissolve the boards of nine state institutions with immediate effect.

The affected institutions are the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company (BOST), Volta Aluminium Company Limited (VALCO), Consolidated Bank Ghana Limited (CBG), Ghana Post Company Limited, Road Maintenance Trust Fund, TDC Ghana Limited, Prestea Sankofa Gold Limited and the National Sports Authority.

The Presidency said the affected boards would be reconstituted in due course, with relevant sector ministers directed to take the necessary steps to give effect to the dissolution.

The board shake-up forms part of a wider reorganisation of the Mahama administration. The President has already made ministerial changes in August, including the reassignment of Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo to Special Initiatives and Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum to the Labour, Employment and Job Creation portfolio. Ernest Brogya Genfi was also reassigned from Deputy Defence Minister to Presidential Advisor on National Resilience and Emergency Preparedness.

The latest notice makes clear that the changes are also intended to reinforce accountability and alignment with the government’s policy priorities.

“All appointees are reminded that public office is a privilege and an opportunity to serve the Ghanaian people,” the statement said.

It further urged appointees to cooperate with the President and commit to delivering the government’s mandate and improving the lives of Ghanaians.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Gunman in deadly Swiss rave attack ‘lone perpetrator’, police say
World.content:
Police say no indication anyone ​else involved in attack that killed 22-year-old Italian woman.

The man suspected of fatally shooting an Italian woman at a rave in Switzerland’s Aarau was a “lone perpetrator”, according to police.

The commander ⁠of the Aargau cantonal police, Michael Leupold, said at a news conference on Wednesday that there was no indication anyone else had been involved in the attack early on Sunday that killed a 22-year-old Italian woman and wounded five people.

“We, therefore, ‌assume with a high degree of certainty that the shooting was the act of one individual,” Leupold said.

The suspect, a 43-year-old Swiss man, handed himself in on Monday to police in Delemont in northwestern Switzerland’s Jura canton and has remained silent while in custody, according to prosecutors.

Leupold said the motive for the attack was not known and the suspect was not previously known to police.

The suspected gunman suffers from “psychological problems” and has maintained his silence since his arrest, Aargau cantonal prosecutor Christoph Ruedi said.

The attack has been met with public shock in Switzerland, where shootings, particularly those involving several victims, are rare despite widespread gun ownership.

Authorities said two pistols and an AK-47 assault rifle were found in the suspect’s car.

The rave’s organisers, meanwhile, said they were “shocked and devastated”, writing on their website that they “will do everything in our power to support the police in their work”.

“A rave should always be a place of joy and love. Never a place where people are killed, injured or left in fear.”
