World.title: Split Landlord’s August Worries Point to Deeper Croatian Tourism Issues
World.content:
September the 1st, 2026 – One Split landlord has shared his August worries about reservations which point to a much deeper problem within Croatian tourism.

A discussion developed on Reddit recently under a post by a resident of Split from Varoš about the bursting of Split’s tourist bubble, prices and “nerve amortisation”.

“Basically, this is the first time it’s happened that I’ve been empty for a longer period in August. I have an apartment in Varoš. So… a week has already passed by without any check-in or reservation made, and my price is low. Is anyone else in a similar situation?” This short post, which an anonymous Split landlord shared on Reddit, instantly laid bare the anxieties that have for some time been creeping among Split’s hospitality workers and property owners. Morski reports that Varoš, a traditional old Split neighbourhood, has experienced unexpected silence right in the very heart the middle of the peak summer season.

stuck between a rock and a hard place – market reality and harsh algorithms…

Many people in the comments immediately pointed out that the problem may not be in Split itself or a general crisis, but in the fact that supply has long exceeded demand. One user vividly explained the situation with the following words: “Supply and demand. In Split there are 15-20% more apartments on the market at any given moment than the city has guests.”

Others located the problem within the digital platforms themselves and suggested the landlord check how the apps treat him at all: “Try searching for your apartment on the site where you rent it out as a guest, preferably in an incognito window… Maybe it’s not even about the price but the algorithm. Most guests don’t scroll past the first 10-15 apartments before booking something.”

A particularly sharp discussion arose around the definition of what exactly a “low price” is, and the mentality of newly minted landlords. Workers from the tourism sector warn that guests have become more cautious and no longer accept just any conditions. “As an employee in a tourist agency, I completely agree with this. All clients who have realistic prices from the start fill up much better, with longer reservations and generally better guests, fewer cancellations, and of course fewer problems.”

Another user described how his family manages to stay competitive, but with enormous effort: “A studio for two 100 euros a night, it’s been full from the May onwards… When Airbnb takes its commission what’s left is quite a bit less than 100, but the occupancy rate is excellent. We clean the place ourselves, greet our guests, wash the bedding… Unfortunately, today everyone would rent out apartments and have a cleaner come, a laundry service… and still make a big profit.”

In contrast to that, landlords from the same neighbourhood appeared on the same post, claiming they have no problems if they position their accommodation well: “I also have an apartment in Varoš… my prices range 150-220 euros and around 400 for Ultra, everything is filled within one day.”

what is the situation with foreign nationals renting purchased properties?

Among the slew of comments, an interesting theory about long-term changes in the structure of guests also stood out. Split and its surroundings are slowly ceasing to be a destination where foreigners exclusively rent accommodation, because many of them have become property owners themselves.

“They count the entry of foreigners into Croatia as visitors, but they don’t count how many of those foreigners already have their own properties located in Croatia. People around Omiš tell me that everything has been bought up by Slovenians, Poles and Austrians. Everyone has sold everything and that’s why the apartments are less filled up. The only ones left are the party crowd that comes to Split every now and then.”

This Reddit post from Varoš actually served as a microcosm of Split’s housing and tourism reality at the moment. While some consider a “week-long hole” in August an anomaly or a bad algorithm, others see it as a fair sobering of a market that has grown for too long on unrealistic foundations. The conclusion of the discussion remains open, but the message is clear: the time when it was enough to “just open the doors” and wait for filling at maximum prices is slowly passing. Split must face the fact that without a sustainable strategy and balancing between the needs of the local population and the real possibilities of supply, empty apartments in August will no longer be a surprise, but the rule.

World.title: Less Heat, Less Crowds, Lower Prices – Croats Travel More in Post-Season
World.content:
September the 1st, 2026 – Less heat, less crowds and generally fairer prices are leading more and more Croats to opt to travel during the post-season.

With the first days of September arriving, the tourist off-season practically officially begins for Croatia. Booking.com has therefore published its 11th annual research report on consumer attitudes and understanding of the social and environmental impact of travel, with insights from 32,500 travellers across 35 markets worldwide. Katarina Kusec reports for Poslovni that according to that data, the majority of Croatian travellers – 58 percent of them in total, plan to travel during the post-season. Both Croatian and European accommodation providers are trying to make use of this period, while the latter want to monetise the remaining demand and attract bookings in the later part of the season.

less heat, less crowds and (sometimes) better value for money

Speaking further about Croats who decide to travel during the off-season, 80 percent of them stated in the research that they do so in order to avoid destinations with large numbers of visitors, while 55 percent are motivated by the possibility of savings. The results indicate that travelling in the off-season has its advantages: besides smaller crowds, there is also a more price-accessible experience, and 53 percent of Croatian travellers plan to avoid overcrowded tourist destinations, which represents an increase of 11 percent compared to the previous year. This part of the season also reflects a more thoughtful approach to travel, as 65 percent of our travellers state that they want to avoid contributing to mass tourism, while 45 percent of those who travel in the off-season are motivated by the desire to reduce pressure on destinations.

the weather is in charge…

As many as 68 percent of all respondents globally say they actively avoid destinations known for extreme weather conditions. Speaking solely about Europeans, research by the European Travel Commission shows that September stands out as an important month for travel, with 22 percent of residents of the Old Continent planning trips in 2025, compared with 25 percent who do so in July and August.

When it comes to owners of accommodation facilities, attention is focused on more commercial tactics with which they can attract demand. Namely, data from the European Accommodation Barometer for 2026 are based on a survey conducted among 1,240 executives and managers from the European accommodation sector, including representatives of hotels and alternative accommodation facilities, and they state that discounts stand out as the most frequently used tool for attracting guests.

In view of this, 79 percent of Croatian accommodation facilities state that special prices or packages for the off-season bring positive results. Accommodation facilities also rely on broader distribution strategies, with 87 percent of them considering online platforms an effective channel for generating bookings in the off-season. The report states that event-driven tourism is another popular way of attracting alternative demand among accommodation facility owners; 37 percent of them stated that they had benefited from event-motivated travel over the past 12 months.

one third cancelled a planned trip

Nevertheless, the weather is increasingly influencing travel, so Booking notes that extreme weather conditions are actively changing travel choices and travel times. Almost three quarters of all respondents said they take into account the risk of extreme weather conditions when choosing a destination (74 percent) and the time of travel (74 percent), while 68 percent say they actively avoid destinations known for extreme conditions.

Interestingly, 31 percent of travellers stated that they had cancelled or changed their travel plans in the past year due to extreme weather conditions or natural disasters.

World.title: Croatia Introduces Life Imprisonment for 15 Criminal Offences
World.content:
September the 1st, 2026 – Croatia is set to introduce life imprisonment for 15 criminal offences as of the 1st of January 2027.

The liability of companies, i.e. legal persons, for criminal offences committed through them by responsible persons will be sanctioned significantly more severely than before. From the 1st of January 2027, life imprisonment in Croatia will be able to be imposed on perpetrators of 15 types of the most serious criminal offences, including those related to irreversible or long-term environmental pollution.

Poslovni reports that the harshest penalty will be able to be imposed on all persons who were 18 or older at the time of committing the offence, which means that younger adults will not be spared either, writes Kristina Turčin for Jutarnji. However, all those sentenced to life imprisonment, regardless of age, will have the right to conditional release after serving 25 years of the sentence.

Specifically, for offences that have caused the most severe environmental pollution, i.e. ecocide, fines will rise to as much as 50 million euros.

Reports (including statements linked to the Ministry of Justice and coverage of the reforms) highlight that life imprisonment will apply to the most serious offences currently punishable by long-term imprisonment. Specific examples repeatedly cited include aggravated/serious murder, femicide, certain forms of genocide, serious forms of human trafficking, sexual abuse and the exploitation of children, terrorist attacks and terrorism-related offences and the aforementioned ecocide.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: Basra records 160 HIV cases;health committee warns of unscreened infections
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — The Health and Environment Committee of the Basra Provincial Council confirmed on Wednesday, September 2, 2026, that official screening and epidemiological monitoring programs have recorded 160 cases of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) in the governorate.

Speaking following a specialized coordination meeting attended by public health directors, epidemiologists, and security representatives, the Deputy Chairman of the Health Committee, Nawfal Al-Mansouri, cautioned that the true count of infections may exceed documented figures due to undetected cases and individuals who have not undergone voluntary testing.

Key Discussion Points and Transmission Risks

Documented Infection Count: Official surveillance registries currently track 160 confirmed HIV cases within Basra Governorate.

Screening Expansion Needs:Al-Mansouri stressed the urgency of expanding confidential early-detection centers and routine health screenings to capture undiagnosed transmissions across vulnerable demographics.

Identified Vectors:In addition to unprotected sexual contact, health authorities highlighted safety violations in unlicensed beauty and cosmetic clinics—such as improper sterilization of micro-needling tools, tattoo implements, and non-medical cosmetic devices—as potential vectors for blood-borne pathogen transmission.

Inter-Agency Security Enforcement: Health inspectors will coordinate with local security services to intensify municipal inspections, shut down unaccredited aesthetic salons, and enforce sanitary licensing compliance across Basra.

Strategic Priorities for Public Health Management

Action Track Strategic Target Operational Steps Diagnostic Access Early diagnosis & case tracking Scaling rapid diagnostic kits at provincial polyclinics and pre-marital screening centers. Commercial Inspection Eliminating unhygienic practices Joint municipal-security raids on unlicensed cosmetic and aesthetic parlors. Therapeutic Protocol Sustaining anti-retroviral access Providing confidential specialized antiretroviral therapy (ART) via Ministry of Health channels. Public Awareness Mitigating social stigma Launching community education initiatives regarding transmission modes and prevention

Al-Mansouri emphasized that managing HIV in the governorate requires a compassionate, preventative, and medical framework rather than punitive or stigmatizing measures.

By coupling widespread public awareness with strict medical sterilization standards in commercial establishments, provincial authorities aim to halt community transmission chains, ensure continuous therapeutic care for patients, and protect general public health.

World.title: Gun found in French lake may unlock Iraqi family murder mystery
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — French detectives are looking into a weapon discovered from Lake Annecy, which might give a fresh clue in the unsolved 2012 murder of British-Iraqi engineer Saad al-Hilli, his family, and a French cyclist.

British holidaymakers discovered the Luger handgun on August 20 in roughly two meters of water near Le Solitaire du Lac, the campground where the al-Hilli family had been camping before to the deaths, according to French magazine Marianne.

The location and kind of weapon have piqued investigators’ attention since the four victims were slain using a Luger P06 handgun, which was formerly used by the Swiss military.

The murder weapon was never found.

Forensic specialists are now investigating the severely damaged pistol to establish if it is a P06 and whether it is related to the murder.

Al-Hilli, an Iraqi-born British citizen from a prominent Iraqi family, was on holiday with his family in the French Alps when he, his wife Iqbal, mother-in-law Suhaila al-Allaf, and cyclist Sylvain Mollier were found shot dead near Chevaline on September 5, 2012.

The couple’s two young girls escaped the deadly assault, with one hiding inside the family’s vehicle for hours before someone found her.

Over the last 14 years, French and British detectives have exvariousiety of possibilities, including familial and financial issues, a random assault, and the likelihood that Mollier was the intended target.

No clear motive or perpetrator has been established.

The finding might be important since detectives have long considered retrieving the murder weapon as a possible way to solve the cold case.

France’s cold-case section in Nanterre has said that the newly recovered handgun may be pertinent to the inquiry.

Investigators must now determine if the pistol is the same type used in the deaths and, more importantly, whether forensic evidence may link it to one of France’s longest-running murder mysteries.

World.title: Iraqi oil shipments surge by 70% in August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two Iraqi energy officials told Reuters that Iraqi oil exports surged by more than 70 percent to around 2.34 million barrels per day in August, compared to approximately 1.35 million barrels per day in July.

The officials explained that the arrival of more oil tankers at southern Iraqi export terminals and the loading of crude oil led to an increase in shipments during August.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, said on Tuesday that the country’s crude oil exports through its southern marine outlets, which link to the Strait of Hormuz, fluctuated between two million and 2.2 million barrels per day in August.

The ministry stressed that these outlets are the major conduit for Iraqi oil exports and a vital part of the national export system.

As part of its attempts to increase the flexibility of the oil export system and minimize dependency on a single route, al-Rikabi stated that the ministry is supporting and developing various alternative export outlets through northern and western Iraq.

Al-Rikabi emphasized that Iraqi oil flows to the Turkish port of Ceyhan are continuing with volumes ranging between 150,000 and 180,000 barrels per day.

Advanced steps are being taken to explore the possibility of increasing oil exports through the Syrian port of Baniyas, according to al-Rikabi. This initiative would offer Iraq an additional outlet to the Mediterranean Sea.

World.title: Baghdad to unify digital customs system across Iraq including Kurdistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Falih Al-Sari has called for expediting customs automation and extending the ASYCUDA system to border crossings in the Kurdistan Region, as Baghdad strives to unify customs operations and boost non-oil income.

During a meeting on customs modernization, al-Sari authorized authorities to start advance payment of customs taxes on October 1, while continuing to develop the Automated System for Customs Data, or ASYCUDA.

The Finance Minister also emphasized the necessity to implement the system at border crossings in the Kurdistan Region, which would integrate federal and regional customs operations under a more unified digital framework.

The move is part of a larger government initiative to replace paper-based customs processes with computerized systems that may increase supervision, speed up clearance, and give authorities with more accurate import and revenue data.

Expanding ASYCUDA throughout Iraq might also help resolve long-standing disagreements between Baghdad and Erbil over customs processes and border income.

A unified system would provide both sides with a standard method for documenting transactions and determining tariffs at border crossings.

The government has increasingly resorted to customs and other non-oil sources to diversify state income and lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

Digital customs systems are also seen as a key instrument for limiting potential for fraud and revenue leakage at border crossings by keeping electronic records of goods, payments, and customs declarations.

Al-Sari’s initiative comes as the Finance Ministry collaborates with other state agencies to electronically connect customs operations to Iraq’s banking and payment infrastructure, enabling fees to be collected and recorded via legitimate financial channels.

The anticipated October 1 implementation of advance customs payments would be another step in that transformation, forcing tariffs to be cleared earlier in the import process rather than depending on customary processes at individual crossings.

Implementing the same system in the Kurdistan Region would be especially important, bringing Iraq closer to a unified national customs framework and perhaps allowing Baghdad and Erbil more control over income produced at the country’s borders.

World.title: Iraq rejects proposal to keep international coalition forces
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has publicly rejected a plan to keep any US-led international coalition forces in Iraq after the September 30, 2026, deadline.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi government, Haider al-Aboudi, said during a press briefing that Baghdad remains strictly committed to the conclusion of the foreign military mission in the country, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Al-Zaidi said earlier that October 1, 2026, will mark a new day in Iraq’s statehood when the country achieves complete sovereignty free of foreign troops.

The military mission of the international coalition will expire on September 30, 2026, and the decision is final and irreversible, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister underscored that October 1 will bring in a new period of total Iraqi independence and full territorial sovereignty, with no foreign military presence.

Iraq’s future interactions with the international coalition’s member states will focus on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared military victory over ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to provide advice and training services at Baghdad’s request.

The official withdrawal of the international coalition follows a bilateral arrangement agreed upon by Baghdad and Washington.

World.title: ‘Reprehensible act of vandalism’: India condemns demolition of century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan, seeks probe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday expressed deep concern over reports of the destruction of a historic Hindu temple in Pakistan's Punjab province and called on the Pakistani government to conduct a prompt and transparent investigation into the incident.

Responding to media queries, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India âunequivocallyâ condemned the reported vandalism of the century-old place of worship in Siraj village in Narowal.

âWe have noted with deep concern the disturbing reports of the destruction of a historic Hindu temple in village Siraj, Narowal, Pakistan. We unequivocally condemn this reprehensible act of vandalism against a century old minority place of worship,â Jaiswal said.

India flags authorities' 'apathy'

The MEA said the apparent failure of authorities to protect the temple was alarming and raised concerns over the safety and religious freedoms of minority communities in Pakistan.

âThe apparent apathy of authorities and failure to protect this century-old temple is alarming. Such incidents are a stark reminder of the continuing vulnerability of minority communities and the egregious violations of their religious freedoms and places of worship in Pakistan,â Jaiswal said.





India called upon Pakistan to investigate the incident and ensure that those responsible are held accountable.

âWe call upon the Government of Pakistan to conduct a prompt and transparent investigation into this incident and ensure that those responsible are held fully accountable,â the MEA spokesperson said.

India also urged Pakistan to take immediate steps to restore the temple and ensure the safety and security of minority communities and their cultural heritage.

âFurthermore, the Government of Pakistan must take immediate remedial measures to restore the desecrated temple and fulfill its primary obligation to guarantee the safety, security and well-being of all its minority citizens and their cultural heritage,â Jaiswal added.

LUCKNOW: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has appointed three new trustees, bringing into its governing body a philanthropist associated with the legacy of late VHP leader Ashok Singhal, a former public representative from Ayodhya and an educationist from Shikohabad whose family has links with the Indian Air Force, the RSS and the erstwhile Jana Sangh.The appointments of Mahesh Bhagchandka, Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav were announced after the Trustâs meeting in Ayodhya on Wednesday. The three have filled vacancies in the Trustâs governing body.Mahesh Bhagchandka, 68, is founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation, is related to Ashok Singhal, one of the prominent figures associated with the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Bhagchandka is also a graduate, businessman based in New Delhi. He is also the author of Hindutva ke Purodha, a book on prominent figures associated with the Hindutva movement.He participated in the rituals as a yajman during both the bhoomi pujan ceremony for the construction of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple and the templeâs pran pratishtha programme. His association with Ram-related cultural initiatives also includes work connected with the Shri Ram Van Gaman Yatra.Bhagchandka has been involved in the installation of Shri Ram Stambhs at 292 sacred sites associated with the route believed to have been taken by Lord Ram during his exile.He is also a member of the executive committee of the World Hindu Economic Forum.His appointment gives the Trust a member with experience in social and cultural initiatives as well as temple-related programmes. He is also related to late Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader Ashok Singhal and is a founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation.Madan Mohan Pandey 74, is a law graduate and advocate based in Ayodhya Cantonment. He represented Shri Ram Lalla Virajman and late Mahant Ramchandra Paramhans Das in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi legal dispute from 1990 to 2019 before the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court.His long association with the temple case places him among those who were directly involved in the legal proceedings that culminated in the Supreme Court judgment paving the way for the construction of the Ram temple at Ayodhya.Pandey also served as Uttar Pradeshâs additional advocate general for six years. Besides his legal practice, he is associated with religious and educational activities. He is the vice-president of the Shri Hari Satsang Samiti and the patron of the Kathakar Yojana training centre in Ayodhya.The third appointee, Nirmala Yadav, comes from a family with a long association with education and public life in Firozabad district. Though the family is originally linked to Uravar village under Sirsaganj tehsil, it has been settled in Shikohabad for several decades. Yadav herself originally hailed from Etah and moved to Shikohabad after her marriage.Yadav served as principal of BDM Girls PG College in Shikohabad from 1999 to 2006. She later became principal of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya (PG) College in Firozabad and retired in 2022.Priyadarshini Upadhaya, the present principal of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya and a former colleague of Yadav, described her as a highly capable administrator. She said Yadav had a strong command over institutional management and was particularly efficient in handling administrative and desk responsibilities.Yadavâs late husband, advocate Harendra Yadav, had served as an RSS district chief. Her father-in-law, Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav, served in the Indian Air Force and was later associated with the Jan Sangh.According to her nephew Sachin Yadav, the familyâs association with education dates back to 1916, when his great-grandfather, Chaudhary Shyam Singh Yadav, founded Kanhai College in Shikohabad. The family also produced a former MLA, Captain Nihal Singh and Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav.
